jobs.description:
Job Description:

About Nextpower

Nextpower is a global leader in intelligent solar tracker and software solutions, optimizing solar power plant performance worldwide.

Within Nextpower, the Robotics and Autonomy team is building and deploying robotic systems that operate at scale in real solar environments. These systems combine perception, planning, control, embedded compute, and cloud infrastructure to increase inspection capacity, improve safety, and enable scalable operations.

We are seeking a Autonomy Engineer to help accelerate the next phase of that growth. This role focuses on advancing real-world autonomy performance across the navigation stack and enabling robots to operate more independently, more efficiently, and at greater scale.

This is a systems-level role spanning perception, planning, and control. You will work directly on robots, in the field and in test environments, to ensure the system performs reliably under real-world conditions.

Role Overview

We are scaling both the capability and deployment of our robotic systems. As autonomy improves, the system must support more robots per operator, operate with higher levels of autonomy across diverse environments, and maintain consistent performance as complexity increases.

This role is focused on building and improving a tightly integrated autonomy stack that works end-to-end on the robot. You will operate within constrained embedded systems where compute, bandwidth, and power are limited, requiring thoughtful tradeoffs in model selection, algorithm design, and system architecture. You will design and implement perception, planning, and control systems, validate them on real hardware, and continuously improve performance through testing, simulation, and data-driven iteration.

You are expected to own system behavior, not just individual algorithms. This means understanding how the full stack behaves in real environments, identifying gaps, and driving improvements that make the system more capable, reliable, and scalable.

Core areas of responsibility include:

  • Developing and improving autonomy capabilities across perception, planning, and control

  • Getting systems working on real robots, not just in simulation

  • Debugging and resolving issues observed in real-world operation

  • Building and using simulation, log replay, and data pipelines to accelerate iteration

  • Collaborating across hardware, integration, and test teams to ensure system-level performance

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field or equivalent relevant professional experience.

  • 5+ years of experience in robotics, autonomy, or related fields, with demonstrated experience developing software for robotic or autonomous systems in real-world environments (not just simulation)

  • Strong proficiency in at least one of the following: C, C++, Python, or Rust

  • Strong experience with Linux command-line environments, Git, and Docker

  • Strong experience with ROS2-based systems

  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to debug complex system behavior

  • Strong hands-on experience working with physical robotic systems

  • Coachable and able to operate effectively within a fast-moving, collaborative team

Preferred Qualifications

  • Developing and deploying perception systems such as:

    • Terrain classification
    • Object detection, recognition, and tracking
    • Semantic understanding of environments
    • Model training, evaluation, deployment, and inference optimization on constrained embedded systems (e.g., CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime)

  • Designing and implementing robot control and planning systems, including:

    • Low-level path control (e.g., Model Predictive Control (MPC))

    • Path planning algorithms such as A*, Dijkstra’s algorithm, or similar

    • Multi-robot planning or coordination

  • Building sensor fusion, filtering, localization, and/or state estimation algorithms, such as:

    • Kalman Filters, Extended Kalman Filters (EKF)

    • Graph-based optimization methods

    • Characterizing sensor and motion noise

  • Working with simulation tools such as Gazebo or similar

  • Using log replay, data pipelines, and performance visualization to debug and improve systems

  • Applying CI/CD, release processes, and test-driven development in robotics systems

  • Debugging networking, remote systems, or communication stacks in deployed environments

  • Operating and deploying systems in outdoor, field robotics environments, including working under compute, bandwidth, and latency constraints

Join Us

At Nextpower, we are building robotic systems that operate at scale in real environments.

As a Senior Autonomy Engineer, you will play a critical role in advancing autonomy capabilities and enabling the next stage of system growth. This is an opportunity to work on real robots, solve real problems, and help scale a system that is already delivering value in the field.

Nextracker offers a comprehensive benefits package. We provide health care coverage, dental and vision, 401(K) participation including company matching, company paid holidays with unlimited paid time off, generous discretionary company bonuses, life and disability protection and more. Employees in certain positions may be eligible for stock compensation. All plans are in accordance with relevant plan documents. For more information on Nextracker’s benefits please view our company website at .

Pay is based on market location and may vary based on factors including experience, skills, education and other job-related reasons. The annual salary range for this position is160K to 190K.

At Nextpower, we are driving the global energy transition with an integrated clean energy technology platform that combines intelligent structural, electrical, and digital solutions for utility-scale power plants. Our comprehensive portfolio enables faster project delivery, higher performance, and greater reliability, helping our customers capture the full value of solar power. Our talented worldwide teams are redefining how solar power plants are designed, built, and operated every day with smart technology, data-driven insights, and advanced automation. Together, we’re building the foundation for the world’s next generation of clean energy infrastructure.

Nextpower is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

We are Nextpower

Payroll Analyst

Locations: Raleigh and Charlotte, North Carolina

Type: Full-time, Fixed-Term (6-12 months with possible extension. Eligible for Benefits)

Job Summary

The Payroll Analyst supports payroll operations by performing payroll audits, reconciliations, exception management, payroll investigations, reporting, data validation, and process improvement activities. This role partners closely with Payroll Specialists, Human Resources, Benefits, Finance, and operational leaders to ensure payroll accuracy, compliance, and operational effectiveness within a complex healthcare environment supporting both union and non-union employees. The Payroll Analyst provides analytical support across Workday Payroll and UKG/Kronos Timekeeping while assisting with payroll testing, work rule validation, leave administration, payroll compliance, and continuous process improvement initiatives.

Responsibilities

Payroll Processing

  • Process and audit bi-weekly, semi-monthly, and special payroll runs, including payroll data validation, balancing, reconciliation, exception review, and resolution of discrepancies before finalization.
  • Administer timekeeping activities in UKG/Kronos, reviewing employee schedules, hours, overtime, shift differentials, premium pay, missing punches, and timecard exceptions. Partner with managers and employees to resolve timekeeping and leave-related issues.
  • Respond to employee payroll inquiries and investigate discrepancies involving paychecks, taxes, deductions, direct deposits, leave balances, and payroll adjustments.
  • Perform payroll reconciliations, review payroll reports and related accounts, and support internal audits, compliance reviews, and month-end and year-end activities.
  • Support payroll tax and garnishment administration, including wage garnishments, levies, tax exceptions, and coordination with ADP for payroll-related filings and compliance documentation.
  • Maintain accurate employee payroll records and validate employee data changes in Workday. Support payroll system updates, enhancements, and process improvements.
  • Participate in testing and implementation of payroll system changes, including union work rules, payroll codes, schedules, and configurations. Perform validation in Workday Sandbox and UKG/Kronos, document results, and support production sign-off.
  • Ensure payroll activities comply with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, internal controls, and confidentiality requirements. Cross-train with team members and support additional payroll projects as needed.

Required System Access

  • Workday Payroll (required)
  • UKG/Kronos Timekeeping (required)
  • ServiceNow

Productivity and Reporting Tools:

  • Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Excel, Word, and SharePoint
  • Payroll reporting tools, employee master data records, and internal process documentation

Eligibility Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Human Resources, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience working with automated payroll systems, preferably in a high-volume U.S. payroll environment.
  • Strong knowledge of end-to-end U.S. payroll processing, including gross-to-net calculations, taxes, deductions, supplemental earnings, benefits, and federal and state payroll requirements.
  • Experience with payroll balancing, reconciliation, employee payroll inquiries, and discrepancy resolution.
  • Experience supporting unionized payroll environments, including union contracts, work rules, schedules, overtime, shift differentials, and premium pay.
  • Healthcare or hospital payroll experience preferred.

Systems and Technical Skills

  • Experience with UKG/Kronos timekeeping systems required; Workday Payroll experience preferred.
  • Experience with ServiceNow preferred. ADP experience is an advantage, particularly payroll tax, garnishments, tax disbursements, quarterly filings, and W-2 support.
  • Experience working with integrated HRIS, payroll, and timekeeping systems.
  • Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills, including VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, Pivot Tables, sorting, filtering, data validation, and reconciliation. Macros and VBA are not required.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to interpret payroll regulations and organizational policies.

Professional Skills

  • Excellent organizational, prioritization, and time management skills.
  • Strong customer service and written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Sound judgment and ability to maintain confidentiality.

Good to Have

  • Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) certification or equivalent.
  • Healthcare payroll experience in a unionized environment.
  • Experience supporting large employee populations, multiple pay groups, high-volume transactions, and complex payroll structures.

jobs.description:
May Mobility is transforming cities through autonomous technology to create a safer, greener, more accessible world. Based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, May develops and deploys autonomous vehicles (AVs) powered by our innovative Multi-Policy Decision Making (MPDM) technology that literally reimagines the way AVs think.

Our vehicles do more than just drive themselves - they provide value to communities, bridge public transit gaps and move people where they need to go safely, easily and with a lot more fun. We’re building the world’s best autonomy system to reimagine transit by minimizing congestion, expanding access and encouraging better land use in order to foster more green, vibrant and livable spaces. Since our founding in 2017, we’ve given more than 500,000 autonomous rides to real people around the globe. And we’re just getting started. We’re hiring people who share our passion for building the future, today, solving real-world problems and seeing the impact of their work. Join us.

Job Summary

The Autonomy Mapping & Localization group builds the spatial intelligence, semantic and topological mapping, and state estimation that let our autonomous vehicles understand where they are and what the world looks like, and we scale that technology safely and reliably to commercial operations serving riders and consumers. We are looking for a Lead ML Engineer to join our team and architect the next generation of our localization stack. As the Lead ML Engineer for Localization, you will build the production-grade feature extraction and state estimation that lets our autonomous vehicles precisely navigate the world's most challenging roads at scale.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Architect and drive the technical roadmap for a production-grade localization machine learning stack, spanning map and sparse landmark-based localization (vision/LiDAR/radar), optimized for real-time performance, robustness against sensor degradation, and integration with the broader autonomy system across diverse Operational Design Domains (ODDs).
  • Lead the research, design, training, and validation of advanced neural architectures. This includes object detection, classification, segmentation, tracking, depth estimation, and 3D reconstruction to extract and model localization features (e.g., traffic signs, pole-like objects, keypoints, edges, signals, and road markings), for robust localization.
  • Drive major feature development from inception to deployment. This includes high-level architecture design, rigorous code reviews, automated testing, mentorship of junior engineers, and technical resolution.
  • Own the end-to-end data strategy for the localization feature extraction domain. You will define data curation, auto-labeling, synthetic data, and active learning pipelines to capture and resolve long-tail scenarios.
  • Develop robust metrics and evaluation frameworks for localization performance, including feature extraction accuracy, temporal consistency, and system-level reliability across diverse ODDs.
  • Define and validate failure mode and degradation criteria for localization features across ODDs, ensuring safety case coverage and graceful fallback behavior under sensor or model failure.
  • Evaluate, adapt, and integrate frontier techniques, including multimodal localization and vision/fusion foundation models, translating research advances into production-ready solutions.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment, translating complex autonomy goals into clear software and system requirements.

Qualifications and Experience

Candidates most successful in this role typically hold the following qualifications or comparable knowledge or experience:

Required

  • Ph.D. or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field with a strong mathematical and engineering foundation.
  • 7+ years of industry experience developing and deploying ML/DL models for computer vision or localization at scale.
  • Deep expertise in several of the following areas:
    • Computer Vision Foundations: Object detection, classification, segmentation, tracking, depth estimation, 3D reconstruction, and feature detection/description (e.g., SIFT, ORB, SuperPoint).
    • Vectorized landmark and feature detection networks, BEV-based scene representation, and temporal modeling.
    • Self-supervised/semi-supervised learning, open-vocabulary detection, and vision/fusion Foundation Models.
  • Experience with feature extraction and/or fusion from imagery, LiDAR, and/or radar.
  • Expertise in ML/DL development using PyTorch or TensorFlow, including experience with synthetic data generation, large-scale dataset handling, data curation, and active learning strategies.
  • Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++ with experience in modular software design and Linux-based development.
  • Expertise in ML optimization for real-time products with limited compute, such as quantization and pruning of large transformer models.
  • Proven leadership in developing technical roadmaps, mentoring engineers, and driving measurable improvements in model performance and system reliability.

Desirable

  • 10+ years of experience in ML/DL for autonomous driving or ADAS systems.
  • Experience utilizing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and/or Foundation Models for auto-labeling and long-tail (edge-case) detection.
  • Working knowledge of localization and state estimation concepts (e.g., SLAM, sensor fusion).
  • A proven record of inventions and/or publication record at top-tier conferences (e.g., CVPR, NeurIPS, ICCV, ECCV, ICLR).

Physical Requirements

  • Standard office working conditions which includes but is not limited to:
    • Prolonged sitting
    • Prolonged standing
    • Prolonged computer use
  • Travel required? - Moderate: 11%-25%

Benefits and Perks

  • Comprehensive healthcare suite including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability plans. Domestic partners who have been residing together at least one year are also eligible to participate.
  • Health Savings and Flexible Spending Healthcare and Dependent Care Accounts available.
  • Rich retirement benefits, including an immediately vested employer safe harbor match.
  • Generous paid parental leave as well as a phased return to work.
  • Flexible vacation policy in addition to paid company holidays.
  • Total Wellness Program providing numerous resources for overall wellbeing
Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and/or people of color are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every qualification. At May Mobility, we’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workforce, so if you’re excited about this role but your previous experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway! You may be the perfect candidate for this or another role at May.

Shape education that supports Australian GPs and better patient care.


Sydney Hybrid or Remote within Australia


We’re looking for an experienced Medical Content Developer to join RX and play a key role across the General Practice Conference & Exhibition (GPCE) and ThinkGP.


This is an opportunity to combine your medical content expertise, editorial judgement and project coordination skills to create high-quality continuing professional development (CPD) education for Australian GPs and primary care professionals.


From accredited online learning modules and quality improvement programs to live conference education, you’ll help ensure our content is clinically credible, practical, engaging and aligned with RACGP and ACRRM accreditation requirements.


About RX

RX is a global events and exhibitions business that creates opportunities for individuals, communities and organisations to connect, learn and do business.


In Australia, our healthcare portfolio brings together face-to-face medical education through GPCE and digital CPD through ThinkGP, providing education and professional development to GPs and other healthcare professionals. We are a leading private provider of CPD education for GPs and healthcare professionals through these two platforms.


ThinkGP is an online platform providing free, accredited CPD education, including modules, clinical audits and advanced courses. Its education is accredited by the RACGP and ACRRM.


Together, our live and digital platforms give you the opportunity to work on education that reaches healthcare professionals across Australia.

As our Medical Content Developer, you’ll sit at the heart of the content development process, helping shape education from initial concept through to final publication and delivery.


Working with clinical experts, medical writers and internal teams, you’ll translate medical evidence, guidelines and educational objectives into clear, relevant and practical learning for busy healthcare professionals.

You’ll work across multiple projects and formats, including ThinkGP online learning and GPCE conference content, balancing clinical accuracy, accreditation requirements, editorial quality and the needs of different stakeholders.


Reporting to the Portfolio Director with a dotted line to the Head of Content, you’ll collaborate closely with the Project Manager, clinical experts, writers, and our editorial, digital and marketing teams.


What you’ll be doing

  • Partner with the Head of Content, clinical experts and medical writers to develop learning outcomes and shape high-quality GP education
  • Translate medical evidence and clinical guidelines into clear, engaging and practical educational content
  • Ensure content meets educational objectives, editorial standards and RACGP/ACRRM accreditation requirements
  • Brief and manage medical writers, establish timelines and provide clear editorial direction throughout development
  • Review, edit and proof CPD activities, conference presentations and supporting educational resources
  • Maintain consistency in clinical accuracy, tone and editorial style across GPCE and ThinkGP
  • Work closely with clinicians and other stakeholders to manage feedback and content revisions
  • Oversee final content uploads and quality assurance within ThinkGP and GPCE systems
  • Identify opportunities to improve workflows and help us efficiently scale our content production

What we’re looking for

You’re an experienced medical or scientific content professional who enjoys turning complex clinical information into education that is accurate, useful and easy to engage with.


You’ll be comfortable working directly with healthcare professionals and subject matter experts, while also having the organisation and attention to detail needed to manage multiple content projects.


You’ll bring:

  • Experience developing medical, clinical or scientific educational content
  • Strong medical writing, editing and proofreading skills across digital and print
  • Confidence interpreting medical evidence and clinical guidelines
  • Excellent project coordination and stakeholder management skills
  • The ability to work collaboratively with clinicians, medical writers and cross-functional teams
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to editorial and clinical accuracy
  • Experience using Microsoft PowerPoint and Word
  • Familiarity with content management systems and Excel
  • Knowledge of RACGP and/or ACRRM accreditation requirements, or the willingness to learn

Experience with Articulate 360 or other e-learning development software would be an advantage.


Why join us?

This is an opportunity to do more than simply write or edit medical content.


You’ll join a small, passionate team where you can influence how GP education is developed and delivered across both digital learning and major live events.


You’ll have the opportunity to:

  • Work across digital and live education, giving you variety beyond a traditional medical writing role
  • Collaborate with clinical experts and turn the latest evidence and guidance into practical education
  • Own content from concept through to delivery, rather than working on just one part of the process

About Partner Forces

Partner Forces is a management consulting firm helping homeland security organizations solve some of their most pressing and complex challenges. We partner with government agencies and industry to strengthen national security and critical infrastructure through expertise in strategy, program management, stakeholder engagement, technology implementation, preparedness, and business transformation.

At Partner Forces, we're more than consultants—we're trusted advisors. We work alongside our clients to solve meaningful problems, deliver actionable solutions, and make a lasting impact. As a growing firm, every employee has the opportunity to contribute not only to our clients' success, but also to the future of Partner Forces. We believe great consultants are developed through collaboration, mentorship, continuous learning, and meaningful opportunities to lead.

Our culture is grounded in six core values: Integrity, Excellence, Positivity, Candor, Determination, and Teamwork. These values shape how we work with our clients, support one another, and grow together. We believe that when our people thrive, our clients do too, which is why we invest in our employees' well-being, professional development, and long-term success.

What we are looking for:

Partner Forces is seeking a Consultant to support strategic communications and stakeholder engagement for a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) client. While strong communications skills are essential, we are first and foremost looking for a relationship builder who can earn the trust of government leaders and become a valued advisor to the client.

The ideal candidate understands that great consulting starts with great relationships. They take the time to understand their client's mission, priorities, challenges, and working style. They know how to listen, ask thoughtful questions, anticipate needs, and bring forward solutions. They are equally comfortable developing executive-level communications, facilitating conversations with diverse stakeholders, and providing candid, thoughtful counsel to client leadership. We're looking for someone who is proactive, personable, collaborative, and low-ego. Someone who can navigate ambiguity, build credibility quickly, and take ownership without needing constant direction. Most importantly, someone who genuinely enjoys working with people and takes pride in being a trusted partner to their clients.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain strong, trusted relationships with government clients, establishing yourself as a go-to advisor for strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, and broader mission priorities.
  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to client leadership, anticipating needs, providing sound recommendations, and helping navigate complex or sensitive communications challenges.
  • Develop and execute strategic communications plans that align with client priorities, mission objectives, and stakeholder needs.
  • Translate complex operational and technical information into clear, compelling messaging for executive, government, and other stakeholder audiences.
  • Draft and refine executive briefings, talking points, presentations, correspondence, reports, and other high-visibility communications products.
  • Coordinate communications across internal teams, government stakeholders, and external partners to ensure consistent messaging and alignment.
  • Support stakeholder engagement activities, including meeting preparation, facilitation, follow-up, and relationship management.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen communications processes, improve information sharing, and enhance stakeholder engagement.
  • Manage competing priorities and time-sensitive deliverables while maintaining exceptional quality, responsiveness, and attention to detail.
  • Navigate sensitive stakeholder dynamics with professionalism, diplomacy, discretion, and sound judgment.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • 5-7 years of experience supporting federal government programs, consulting engagements, or related project management efforts.
  • Experience supporting DHS or other federal civilian agencies.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and sustain trusted relationships with government clients, including advising senior leaders and navigating complex stakeholder environments.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence, with the ability to connect with diverse personalities, build credibility, and influence without formal authority.
  • Strong strategic communications experience, including executive messaging, stakeholder communications, briefing development, and communications planning.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex information into clear, actionable messaging.
  • A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset with the ability to anticipate client needs, exercise sound judgment, and take initiative.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities and tight deadlines.
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity, sensitive situations, and shifting client priorities with professionalism and diplomacy.
  • A collaborative, low-ego approach and genuine commitment to exceptional client service.
  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DHS suitability determination or security clearance, as required.

Next Steps:

If your application looks like a match, someone from our People Operations team will reach out to schedule a phone screening. During this conversation, we will determine if the current or future position aligns with your experience and skills. If things go well, from there you'll meet with members from the project team, including the hiring manager and teammates, and possibly be asked to submit a writing assessment to showcase your practical knowledge. If we find you are a match, you’ll get a call offering you the role. While we wish we could hire every great candidate who comes our way, the reality is that we can't. If you are not selected, we will be sure to connect with you and let you know so you can move on with your search. We will also keep your resume for future needs.

Salary Range & Compensation Philosophy

The anticipated salary range for this position is $95,000 - $120,000. At Partner Forces, we recognize that every candidate brings a unique combination of skills, experiences, and qualifications. Compensation decisions consider several factors, including years of relevant experience, specialized expertise, clearance level, and the requirements of the role. We also believe compensation is a starting point, not a finish line. We're committed to recognizing contributions, rewarding strong performance, and creating opportunities for continued growth as our employees develop their skills and careers at Partner Forces.

Partner Forces is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityCompliance at SEC- and FINRA-regulated firms still runs on manual review and noisy keyword tools, and the costs are rising.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Compliance at SEC- and FINRA-regulated firms still runs on manual review and noisy keyword tools, and the costs are rising.

  • Legacy surveillance tools generate hundreds of false positives every week.

  • A typical 5-person team loses ~3,000 hours a year to triage and status chasing, about $250K in leakage per mid-market firm.

  • Recent SEC penalties for off-channel communication and recordkeeping failures topped $536M.

  • Market: 19,000 US RIAs and broker-dealers, 7,800 mid-market targets, ~$500M SAM at a $40K ACV.

The Venture

Backed by AI venture builder FutureSight, FinLext is building a compliance operations platform for broker-dealers, registered investment advisers, and wealth managers. We help compliance teams handle more review work, resolve issues faster, and retain the evidence behind their decisions. Compliance professionals keep final approval authority.

Our initial focus is marketing review: helping firms review marketing materials and client communications before publication. The product brings together submitted content, applicable rules, firm policies, proposed corrections, and reviewer decisions in one workflow. Managed and controlled AI and LLMs deliver consistent and differentiating analysis in moments, not hours or days.

The value to customers is concrete:

  • Fewer rounds of revision before approval. Reviewers receive findings tied to specific passages, supporting sources, and proposed corrections. Marketing teams and advisors get actionable feedback that helps them move submissions toward approval.

  • More capacity for compliance teams. AI handles repeatable first-pass analysis and prepares findings for review. Compliance professionals can spend more time assessing substantive concerns and exercising judgment–helping grow their firms rather than performing mundane reviews.

  • Recommendations reviewers can inspect. Each finding connects the content under review to the relevant rule or firm policy. Reviewers can assess the reasoning, challenge the recommendation, and make an informed decision.

  • More Reliable and Consistent Decisions. Better, faster decisions mean fewer fines, better audit outcomes, and much higher user satisfaction.

Marketing review gives us a focused starting point for demonstrating customer value. The broader opportunity is to connect related compliance work, including electronic communications and trading oversight. Underlying these process transformations is regulatory intelligence incorporating law, regulations, interpretations and firm policy.

Backed by AI venture builder FutureSight, FinLext is the compliance operations platform for broker-dealers, RIAs and wealth managers: one auditable system for regulatory intelligence, supervisory review, remediation, human approval and retained records. AI creates capacity and consistency; compliance professionals keep authority. Our moat is a high-trust architecture and superior outcomes, not generic AI.

The Partnership

FinLext was founded by Richard Hulit (ex-Boomi, Appian, FIS, Nasdaq OMX), supported by an advisory board of ex-regulators, CCOs and legal counsel. The market work is done; now we need a technical and product co-founder to lead the build.

This is a Technical and Product co-founder role. You receive founder-level equity, co-decision rights on product, technology, hiring, fundraising and strategy, a board or observer seat as the stage allows, and a genuine partnership with the CEO on every material decision.

Role & Responsibilities

You will define how AI, software, and professional judgment work together in a regulated environment. That includes the underlying platform and the interfaces compliance teams use to delegate work, inspect findings, request revisions, and make decisions.

For a technical co-founder, this means owning the product and architecture from the outset. You will turn customer discovery into production software and solve practical problems in AI reliability, source grounding, and secure enterprise workflows. Working alongside an experienced financial technology founder and compliance advisors, you will shape both the first product and the business it becomes.

The build spans three connected areas:

  • Agentic product experiences. Design interfaces where users can assign review work, follow its progress, inspect supporting evidence, and act on proposed corrections. Determine where agents can analyze, research, or route work independently, and where they need clarification or human intervention. Make uncertainty and decision ownership visible, with compliance professionals retaining final approval.

  • Applied AI and orchestration. Build systems that interpret submitted content against relevant regulations and firm policies, retrieve supporting sources, and produce useful findings and proposed revisions. Own model selection, retrieval, tool use, and cross-task coordination. Establish evaluations for missed issues, unsupported findings, citation accuracy, and reviewer acceptance, alongside latency and cost.

  • The platform behind the workflow. Architect the services for document ingestion, versioning, workflow state, permissions, and retained decision history. Build secure customer boundaries and integrations with firms’ existing systems. Develop the observability and recovery mechanisms needed to understand failures, reproduce results, and operate reliably as usage grows.

Marketing review provides a focused first application. The broader engineering opportunity is to build reusable capabilities for evidence, policy interpretation, agent execution, and human review that can support additional compliance workflows. Initial work is underway; you will own final design and platform delivery.

You will own these product and architecture decisions, working directly with customers and domain experts to establish what earns trust and delivers measurable value.

As Technical and Product Co-founder, you will own both how we build and what we build.

  • Architecture: write the first production code and design the bounded agent system and its orchestration.

  • AI/LLM: own model strategy, RAG over SEC/FINRA rules and firm policy, private deployment where needed, and continuous evaluation.

  • Explainability and reliability: every verdict cites its rule; build the evidence ledger, observability and regression testing so results hold up in the field.

  • Security: SOC 2 readiness, tenant isolation, encryption and audit logging from day one.

  • Product Sense: turn discovery and pilot feedback into a sharp vision and wedge; design human-in-the-loop workflows CCOs trust; decide where AI acts, suggests or only observes.

  • Execution: own the roadmap and prioritization from MVP to GA; scope ruthlessly, ship weekly with design partners and convert pilots into paying customers.

  • Analytical: define and instrument success metrics (review time saved, false-positive reduction, accuracy, override rate); quantify customer ROI to support pricing, sales and fundraising.

  • Team: hire and lead the founding engineering and applied-AI team and set its culture.

Your first 18 months

  1. Months 1–3: ship the Marketing Review + Evidence Ledger MVP with 2–3 signed pilots.

  2. Months 4–6: convert 1–2 pilots to paying customers with proven ROI and auditability.

  3. Months 7–9: release GA v1, adding communications and trade surveillance and audit reporting.

  4. Months 10–18: expand into regulatory filings and enterprise integrations; reach 10+ paying customers and $1M ARR.

Co-Founder Profile

You are a builder who has shipped AI into production where wrong answers had real consequences, and who thinks as hard about the product as about the code.

  • Shipped LLM-powered systems into production where incorrect outputs carried real consequences, not prototypes or demos.

  • Full-stack depth across applied LLMs, RAG and retrieval, agent orchestration, deterministic rules engines, human-in-the-loop workflows and observability.

  • Experience building secure multi-tenant SaaS: SOC 2, tenant isolation, encryption, audit logging.

  • Strong product sense: you have defined what to build from customer discovery and owned a roadmap, not just executed one.

  • Bias towards action: you ship fast, cut scope ruthlessly and make decisive calls with imperfect information.

  • Analytical rigour: you define metrics, build evaluations and let data settle debates.

  • Well-formed convictions about explainability and reliability, developed in production.

  • Ready to operate as a principal: setting the agenda, owning outcomes, and representing FinLext to customers, partners and investors as its technical and product voice.

Strongly Preferred

  • Prior early-stage Technology and Product co-founder experience.

  • Background in RegTech, legal tech, fintech compliance, healthcare or another high-trust regulated vertical.

  • Familiarity with US wealth management and SEC/FINRA workflows: marketing review, communications surveillance, trade monitoring, books-and-records.

  • Hands-on experience self-hosting or privately deploying foundation models.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

You will have full responsibility for the team's sales performance, revenue targets and execution, leading a team of Account Managers to identify, develop and close expansion opportunities. You will own the Expansion sales strategy, drive operational excellence and build a high-performing team that consistently delivers against its targets.

Working closely with the Regional Sales Director and the broader leadership team, you will play a key role in shaping and executing the regional business strategy, strengthening our market presence and accelerating growth.

This is a hands-on sales leadership role in a high-growth environment, requiring strong commercial acumen, a growth mindset, resilience, and the ability to translate strategy into execution.

Sales Leadership & Revenue Growth

  • Own and drive the Expansion sales strategy and execution across the Central region, ensuring consistent delivery against quarterly and annual revenue targets.

  • Lead, manage and inspire a high-performing team of Account Managers, taking accountability for their sales performance, productivity and development.

  • Drive a strong sales culture focused on revenue growth, customer value, accountability and consistent execution.

  • Identify and accelerate expansion opportunities across the existing customer base through upsell, cross-sell and strategic account growth.

  • Drive rigorous sales execution, including pipeline generation, opportunity management, deal strategy, negotiation and closing.

  • Own sales forecasting, pipeline management and reporting, ensuring accuracy, transparency and proactive risk management.

  • Actively support the team on strategic and complex opportunities to maximise deal progression and closing success.

Strategy & Go-to-Market Execution

  • Partner closely with the Regional Sales Director and leadership team to define and execute the overall regional business strategy.

  • Develop and implement regional sales plans and go-to-market strategies to maximise growth potential across the customer base.

  • Identify opportunities to improve sales productivity, commercial performance and execution.

  • Build strong relationships with key customers and executive stakeholders, supporting the team in developing strategic partnerships and unlocking growth opportunities.

  • Stay close to market developments, industry trends and competitors to identify new opportunities.

People Leadership & Talent Development

  • Recruit, onboard and develop top sales talent, building a strong and scalable Expansion Sales organisation.

  • Provide continuous coaching, feedback and performance management to strengthen individual and team capabilities.

  • Establish clear performance expectations and foster a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

  • Act as a role model and cultural ambassador, fostering an inclusive and high-performance working environment.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Build strong partnerships with New Business Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, Solution Engineering and other cross-functional teams to ensure an aligned go-to-market approach.

  • Leverage internal resources effectively, including MRE, Business Development, Pre-Sales, Support, Project Management and Product Marketing, to maximise sales effectiveness and achieve revenue goals.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment to ensure customer opportunities are identified, developed and converted effectively.

  • Represent the company's vision, products and values at customer meetings, industry events and conferences.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree desirable.
  • You have 5+ years of experience in building and leading a sales team within a SaaS environment.
  • You are able to develop and execute a top-tier vision and go-to-market strategy.
  • You have strong experience working with Enterprise Customers.
  • You understand and drive the strategic development of the existing customer base.
  • You understand how to collaborate, leverage, and develop the partner ecosystem to increase and accelerate sales footprint in the marketplace.
  • You speak fluent German and English.
  • You are an inspiring leader! You have a desire to develop and lead your teams by example.
  • You and your team consistently achieve and overachieve sales goals and targets.
  • You are an excellent communicator - you know what to say and, more importantly, how and when to say it.
  • You are willing to go the extra mile with a strong work ethic.
  • You are self-motivated, resourceful, and resilient.

The role can be based either at our Berlin office on a hybrid model for candidates based in Berlin (3 fixed days: Monday, Wednesday & Thursday), or 100% remote from anywhere in Germany for candidates based outside of Berlin.

jobs.excerpt: Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies.
jobs.description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

About the Role

Parachute Health is hiring a Staff Engineer to join our Eligibility & Benefits team. We build the systems that ensures every durable medical equipment (DME) order has verified coverage before it ships. In this role, you’ll tackle real-time payer eligibility checks and architect solutions to parse messy, inconsistent insurance data, directly cutting claim denials and eliminating manual overhead for DME providers.

Responsibilities

  • Develop in an agile environment, including TDD and flexible pair programming.
  • Work every day with Product and Design to scope features, weigh tradeoffs, and turn workflows into software that’s simple to use and holds up in production.
  • Direct key technical decisions related to application and data model design.
  • Maintain stable and performant application stacks.
  • Ship quality code that moves the business. Deliver readable, well-tested, maintainable code tied to clear outcomes for clinicians, suppliers, and patients.
  • Understanding of data structures, TDD, and software engineering design patterns and principles.
  • Ability to lead a team in making technical decisions.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation, ensuring timely resolution of critical system issues, and contributing to the continuous improvement of our system reliability and availability.
  • Use AI developer tools to work smarter. Adopt and help evaluate AI coding assistants and automation that speed up delivery, catch defects earlier, and cut repetitive work.
  • Own integrations with payers and clearinghouses, including retries, failure modes, and keeping data current.
  • Design how payer and plan data gets mapped, measure how accurate it is against what suppliers actually bill, and get it better.
  • Partner with Product, Ops, and supplier stakeholders, and write the technical narrative that gets the org aligned.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 7 years of experience in a production environment with Ruby on Rails or other open source languages (e.g., Python, Golang, JavaScript)
  • Staff-level engineering experience, including technical leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and mentoring engineers
  • Revenue cycle experience in at least one of: eligibility and benefits, claims, billing, or prior authorization
  • Must reside in the U.S.

Nice to Have

  • Familiar with AWS services (EC2, ECS, S3, RDS, etc).
  • Exposure to X12 EDI: 270/271, 837/835, 278
  • Clearinghouses or revenue cycle vendors: Availity, Change Healthcare/Optum, Waystar, Stedi, Experian Health

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage: Comprehensive plans with options for low-to-no-cost premiums.
  • Employer HSA Contribution: Company-funded contributions to your Health Savings Account.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan
  • Equity Incentive Plan
  • Annual Company-Wide Bonus: Opportunity for up to 15% bonus based on company performance.
  • Remote-First Culture: We are remote-first with a dedicated NYC office and reimbursement options for co-working spaces.
  • Flexible Vacation Policy
  • Summer Fridays: 5 additional Fridays off during the summer (separate from PTO).
  • Home Office and Wellness Stipend
  • Monthly Internet Stipend
  • Annual Learning and Development Stipend

Base Salary Band (based on experience and level)

$200,000 - $260,000

Job Summary:

The Sales Operations & Analytics Associate provides analytical, systems and operational support to the Business Development and wider Commercial organization. The role is responsible for developing dashboards and performance reporting, supporting pipeline and forecasting processes, and improving the commercial workflows that underpin effective decision-making.

Working closely with Business Development, Commercial Leadership, Finance, Marketing and other cross-functional stakeholders, the role translates commercial data into clear, actionable insight. It also helps ensure that Salesforce processes, reporting definitions and data standards are applied consistently across the organization.

The successful candidate will combine strong analytical capability with practical Salesforce experience, attention to detail and a continuous-improvement mindset. They will be comfortable investigating data issues, developing reporting solutions, documenting processes and supporting commercial users in maintaining complete, accurate and timely information.

Main Responsibilities:

1). Commercial Analytics & Reporting

  • Develop and maintain dashboards, KPI scorecards and commercial reporting for Business Development and Leadership.
  • Analyze pipeline, forecasting, bookings, conversions and performance trends to provide actionable business insights.
  • Deliver recurring and ad hoc reporting that supports strategic decision-making.
  • Identify risks, opportunities and performance gaps through data analysis.
  • Utilize Salesforce, Excel, Power BI and other BI tools to improve reporting and visibility.

2). Salesforce Administration & CRM Management

  • Serve as a key Salesforce resource supporting Business Development and Commercial teams.
  • Develop and maintain Salesforce reports, dashboards, workflows and system enhancements.
  • Gather business requirements and translate them into scalable CRM solutions.
  • Support CRM projects including testing, integrations, user administration and data migrations.

3). Data Governance & Quality

  • Maintain CRM data standards, governance processes and quality controls.
  • Conduct data audits, validation reviews and remediation activities to improve data integrity.
  • Partner with stakeholders to resolve data issues and improve reporting accuracy.
  • Implement controls, automation and process improvements that reduce recurring data-quality issues.

4). Pipeline, Forecasting & Commercial Operations

  • Support pipeline management, forecasting and commercial performance reviews.
  • Monitor opportunity movement, ageing, conversion and forecast accuracy.
  • Prepare analysis and reporting for leadership reviews and commercial meetings.
  • Identify bottlenecks, risks and inconsistencies affecting forecast reliability.
  • Support account planning, territory management and commercial prioritization activities.

5). Process Improvement & Cross-Functional Support

  • Lead initiatives that improve commercial processes, reporting efficiency and operational effectiveness.
  • Document workflows, SOPs and best practices while maintaining process governance.
  • Evaluate and implement automation opportunities that reduce manual effort.

Minimum Education & Experience:

  • 5+ Years experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Commercial Operations, CRM Administration, Business Analytics or a related function.
  • Hands-on experience supporting Salesforce and commercial reporting processes.
  • Experience developing dashboards, reports and performance metrics for business stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and provide actionable insights.
  • Understanding of CRM data governance, data quality standards and process compliance.
  • Experience supporting pipeline management, forecasting and commercial performance reviews.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills; experience with Power BI, Tableau or similar BI tools preferred.
  • Ability to work effectively across Business Development, Marketing, Finance and Operations teams.

Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies:

  • Advanced knowledge of sales operations, commercial processes, pipeline management, forecasting methodologies, and CRM best practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex data sets, identify trends, and translate findings into actionable business recommendations.
  • Proficiency in Salesforce administration, reporting, dashboard development, workflow management, and CRM optimization.
  • Expertise in data visualization and business intelligence tools, including advanced Microsoft Excel and Power BI (or comparable analytics platforms).
  • Knowledge of data governance principles, data quality management practices, and controls that ensure reporting accuracy and integrity.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining accurate, complete, and reliable commercial and operational data.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, conduct detailed investigations, and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced business environment.
  • Effective stakeholder management and collaboration skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally across Business Development, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Leadership teams.
  • Process improvement mindset with experience identifying inefficiencies, implementing automation opportunities, and driving operational excellence.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present data, insights, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

jobs.excerpt: ROLE TITLE: Managing Director, Public Relations, Earned Media & High-Stakes Communications (Full time) POSITION REPORTS TO: Vice President, Public Relations, Earned Media & High-Stakes Communications APPLICATION DEADLINE: Sunday, November 8, 2026 LOCATION: Remote/Flexible WHAT YOU’LL DOThe Managing Director of Communications & Public Affairs plays a senior, strategic role in shaping and executing Teach For America’s earned media strategy across both regional markets and key national priority areas.
jobs.description:
ROLE TITLE: Managing Director, Public Relations, Earned Media & High-Stakes Communications (Full time)

POSITION REPORTS TO: Vice President, Public Relations, Earned Media & High-Stakes Communications

APPLICATION DEADLINE: Sunday, November 8, 2026

LOCATION: Remote/Flexible

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The Managing Director of Communications & Public Affairs plays a senior, strategic role in shaping and executing Teach For America’s earned media strategy across both regional markets and key national priority areas. Reporting to the Vice President of Communications & Public Affairs, this role is responsible for setting earned media direction nationwide by supporting regions while also partnering closely with national teams to develop and execute media strategies that advance org wide priorities and ensure Teach For America shows up clearly, accurately, and credibly in local and national media.


This is a high‑judgment, high‑impact role that combines strategy, execution, and counsel. You lead earned media planning across regions and national partners, prioritize markets and storylines, and guide teams through both proactive campaigns and high‑stakes reactive moments. You bring a strong point of view on narrative, risk, and opportunity and use it to influence how Teach For America is positioned across communities and in the media nationwide. As a trusted partner to regional and national leaders, you help teams identify the stories that matter most, prepare leaders to serve as effective messengers, and navigate complex or sensitive media situations. The goal of this role is not just to land coverage but to ensure earned media meaningfully advances organizational priorities, strengthens public trust, and supports Teach For America’s mission at both the local and national level.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

Lead Regional Earned Media Strategy & Execution (45%)

  • Develop and lead 4–5 earned media campaigns annually that advance organization‑wide priorities and messaging, integrating both regional and national pitch opportunities.
  • Design and drive regional earned media strategies aligned to earned media campaigns, organizational priorities, and the broader narrative goals of Teach For America.
  • Set clear priorities across regions, determining where to invest proactive outreach based on impact, opportunity, and risk.
  • Oversee the execution of earned media campaigns across regional markets, ensuring coverage is timely, high‑quality, and strategically aligned.

Serve as Senior Counsel to Regional & National Teams (30%)

  • Serve as a senior strategic partner to both regional teams and national partners, including Growth, Development, and the Reinvention Lab, to develop and execute earned media strategies that advance organizational priorities.
  • Lead the development of pitches and story strategies for both local and national outlets, tailoring approaches based on audience, market, and moment.
  • Advise national teams on earned media strategy, narrative development, and positioning in support of their goals.
  • Surface and assess reputational and external affairs risks, partnering with leaders to navigate sensitive, high‑visibility, or complex media situations.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to regional staff and leaders on media strategy, messaging, and spokesperson readiness.
  • Partner with teams to identify compelling storylines, sharpen narratives, and prepare leaders to serve as effective media messengers.

Lead Reactive & High‑Stakes Communications (15%)

  • Manage and support responses to incoming media inquiries, particularly during time‑sensitive or high‑stakes moments.
  • Apply sound judgment and strategic thinking to assess risk, recommend approaches, and ensure consistency with organizational values and messaging.
  • Coordinate closely with internal partners to align responses and mitigate reputational risk.

Strengthen Systems, Insights & Cross‑Team Alignment (10%)

  • Track, analyze, and synthesize regional media activity to inform strategy, identify trends, and share insights across the communications team.
  • Partner with colleagues responsible for owned channels, internal communications, and key audiences to ensure earned media is effectively shared and amplified.
  • Contribute to the ongoing evolution of earned media practices, tools, and standards across regions.

A WEEK IN THE LIFE

In a typical week, you might be advising multiple regions on earned media strategy tied to a national campaign, prioritizing which markets to lean into and why. You could be coaching an executive director ahead of a sensitive interview, responding to a fast‑moving media inquiry, or helping a regional team sharpen a story angle to better advance Teach For America’s narrative.

Your work balances proactive planning with real‑time decision‑making. As news cycles shift and regional needs emerge, you adjust strategy, offer clear counsel, and ensure teams are supported with the guidance and structure they need to move quickly and thoughtfully.

YOUR EXPERIENCE

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8 - 10+ years of related experience in communications, journalism, public relations, or a related field
  • Demonstrated experience executing earned media efforts, including pitching reporters and supporting media interviews
  • Experience supporting reactive or high‑stakes communications situations
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a deadline‑driven environment
  • Ability to work collaboratively with cross‑functional and geographically dispersed teams
  • Strong alignment with Teach For America’s mission, values, and commitment to educational excellence for all students

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience working with regional or local media markets
  • Familiarity with the education sector or nonprofit communications
  • Experience preparing senior leaders or staff as media spokespeople
  • Comfort working behind the scenes to execute communications plans developed by senior leaders
  • Work Demands: This is a full‑time role. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required. Limited travel may be expected on an ad hoc basis.

YOUR FUTURE TEAM

Teach For America’s Communications & Public Affairs team shapes the organization’s public voice and works in close partnership with regional and national teams to elevate stories from across our network and mitigate external risk. The earned media team focuses on securing timely, high‑quality coverage that reflects the experiences of students, teachers, and communities and supports Teach For America’s broader mission.

Who we are

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role

Samsara's Recruiting Operations team runs the engine behind every hire, from the moment a req opens to the day an offer is signed. We're looking for a Senior Manager to own that engine end to end: leading our Recruiting Coordination Manager and two Recruiting Operations Managers, and driving the AI-powered transformation that will make hiring at Samsara faster and sharper for years to come.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.

  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the vision and strategy for all of Recruiting Operations end to end, from req management through scheduling to offer approval
  • Lead the function through a Recruiting Coordination Manager and two Recruiting Operations Managers, building each of their capability to run their part of the system while you focus on strategy and escalations
  • Lead Samsara through a major recruiting technology transformation over the next year: use AI to rebuild how the team works, not just automate a step, and own the change management that makes it stick
  • Refine the operating model for recruiting operations, elevating team delivery while automation and AI take over manual administrative tasks
  • Use data and insights to set goals, track progress, and influence decisions, partnering with recruiting and business executive leadership so strategy, tooling, and reporting support the broader talent roadmap
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team). Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • At least 8 years of experience in recruiting operations, recruiting coordination, or a closely related recruiting or HR related role
  • At least 5 of those years in a formal people-leadership role, including experience managing people-managers
  • A builder's mindset with AI and automation: has tested, prototyped, or built tools or workflows themselves, and can speak concretely to what worked and what didn't
  • Has led a team through a major recruiting technology transition, change management included, not just the technical rollout
  • Has used data to run a recruiting operations or coordination function, and can name a specific decision that data changed
  • Based remotely within the US

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Working knowledge of LLM APIs, prompt engineering, or AI-augmented workflows, enough to know where AI genuinely helps versus where it's just novelty
  • Direct experience with HR and recruiting platforms
  • A track record of measurably improving candidate or employee experience at scale
  • Has defined baselines and measured the before-and-after impact of a process or automation change
  • Strong executive stakeholder management skills across Recruiting, PeopleTech, and Business partners

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

You’ll be accountable for making sure our AI and data investments deliver measurable business results and a lasting competitive advantage.

Architecture and standards

  • Own the enterprise target architecture for data and AI, and publish and maintain reference architectures, standards and decision records
  • Set architectural principles: modularity, API-first design, interoperability, reuse, portability and lifecycle management
  • Decide what’s central by default, what becomes central once reuse is proven, what stays with business units, and what’s jointly owned
  • Give clear guidance on which technologies, models and patterns to use for which job
  • Keep a forward-looking view of AI technologies, vendors, models and frameworks

Agentic AI platform

Data architecture

  • Define the split between central standards and business-unit domain models, and review those models for consistency
  • Define the technical criteria for data readiness used in product planning
  • Work with Legal and Privacy on the data architecture for our industry insights product, covering rights, aggregation, consent and lineage

Standards for AI-assisted development

  • Turn standards into context that AI coding agents use: repository instruction files, reusable skills and prompts, MCP tool definitions and starter templates
  • Build architecture rules into CI: policy as code, fitness functions, scans on AI-generated code, and evaluation gates before release
  • Define what coding and runtime agents can do in each environment, including tool allow-lists, least-privilege access, no secrets or card data in prompts or logs, and human review based on risk
  • Set patterns for wrapping legacy products with MCP and for AI-assisted migration
  • Track delivery metrics such as PR-to-production rate, rework within 21 days, change failure rate and AI cost per accepted change

Security, privacy and responsible AI

  • Work with the AI Security Architect, CISO, Legal and Privacy to build security into every reference architecture: threat models, least privilege, tenant isolation, prompt-injection defences and server-side action validation
  • Make sure the architecture supports data residency, tenant isolation, retention, deletion and contractual data-use limits
  • Assess risks from model providers, external AI services, open-source models, training data, dependencies and third-party integrations

Cost, observability and reliability

  • Design cost control into the platform: cost tracking by business unit, product and workflow, token and latency budgets, caching and kill switches
  • Optimise token use, model choice, context size, retrieval efficiency and compute
  • Define a standard telemetry schema in Datadog covering outcome, quality, cost and security signals
  • Set service-level objectives for central platform services

Governance and vendors

  • Set up an AI and data governance framework covering ownership, accountability, decision rights, data quality and escalation
  • Chair the fortnightly Data and AI Architecture, Security and Risk Council, and present trade-offs to the Executive AI Steering group
  • Lead technical evaluation of AI platforms, models and data tools, and reduce overlap and lock-in (one gateway, abstraction layers, a tested exit plan)
  • Set technical standards for consultants, including code in Xplor repos, pairing with our engineers and knowledge transfer

Leadership and mentoring

  • Advise the Chief AI Officer on architecture, technology investment and emerging risk, in business terms
  • Lead the community of business-unit architects and mentor engineers, with scope to grow a small team of 2 to 3 architects

This position has an annual base salary range of $173,000 to $193,000 USD.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in the U.S., excluding Hawaii and Alaska. We’d prefer candidates in the Eastern or Central time zones.

What would make me a good candidate?

  • 15+ years in software, data, AI or platform engineering, including at least 7 as an enterprise or principal architect
  • You’ve taken LLM or agentic systems into production at scale, and you know what it takes: orchestration, retrieval, evals, guardrails, model routing and observability
  • Deep experience in enterprise data architecture, ideally on Snowflake, including semantic layers, governed metrics, data modelling, entity resolution, data quality and lineage
  • You’ve designed multi-tenant SaaS platforms with strict tenant isolation and identity propagation
  • You’ve worked with regulated data and know how to design for compliance from the start
  • You’ve led architecture across multiple products or business units, ideally after acquisitions, where you had to bring together a mix of modern and legacy technology
  • You still write production code, and engineers respect your code reviews
  • You’ve set up architecture governance (review boards, standards, waivers) that teams actually used rather than worked around
  • You understand the cost side of AI, including token budgets, cost per task and FinOps for AI workloads
  • You can explain technical trade-offs to executives and the board in plain business terms

It would be great if you also have

  • Hands-on production experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP), agent frameworks or an LLM gateway
  • Led a build-vs-buy decision for an AI platform, including contract, IP and exit terms
  • A background in vertical SaaS
  • Experience with Datadog or similar observability tools for AI systems, and OpenTelemetry
  • Familiarity with AI risk frameworks such as NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001, and the EU AI Act
  • Experience with data residency and privacy rules across AU, NZ, US, UK and EU

jobs.title: Chief Experience Officer (CXO)
jobs.excerpt: 1.  Role SummaryThe Chief Experience Officer (CXO) is responsible for developing and executing the organization's overall experience strategy across customer, client, employee, and stakeholder touchpoints.
jobs.description:
1. Role Summary

The Chief Experience Officer (CXO) is responsible for developing and executing the organization's overall experience strategy across customer, client, employee, and stakeholder touchpoints. The role focuses on building a customer-centric culture, improving service quality, strengthening customer relationships, and ensuring consistent, seamless, and positive experiences across all insurance and investment products and services.

The CXO will lead customer experience (CX), service delivery, customer engagement, and experience transformation initiatives. The position will work closely with business, operations, technology, sales, marketing, claims, underwriting, and investment teams to improve satisfaction, loyalty, retention, and long-term business performance.

2. Key Responsibilities

Customer Experience Strategy

  • Develop and implement an enterprise-wide customer experience strategy aligned with the organization's business objectives.
  • Establish a customer-first culture across insurance, investment, and financial service operations.
  • Define customer experience standards, service principles, and performance benchmarks.
  • Identify opportunities to differentiate the organization through superior customer service and engagement.

Customer Journey Management

  • Map and optimize end-to-end customer journeys across product discovery, onboarding, policy issuance, premium payments, claims, renewals, investment services, and account management.
  • Identify service gaps, customer pain points, and process inefficiencies.
  • Simplify customer interactions and reduce friction across digital and traditional service channels.
  • Ensure consistent experiences across branches, call centres, websites, mobile applications, and relationship management teams.

Customer Satisfaction and Retention

  • Develop initiatives to improve customer satisfaction, loyalty, retention, and lifetime value.
  • Monitor customer feedback, complaints, service requests, and customer sentiment.
  • Establish customer feedback mechanisms, including surveys, NPS, CSAT, and customer interviews.
  • Lead initiatives to reduce customer attrition and improve policy renewal and investment account retention rates.

Digital Experience and Innovation

  • Collaborate with technology and digital teams to improve online platforms, mobile applications, customer portals, and self-service solutions.
  • Drive digital adoption and improve accessibility of insurance and investment services.
  • Leverage customer analytics, automation, AI, and CRM platforms to personalize customer interactions.
  • Champion innovative solutions that improve customer convenience and operational efficiency.

Customer Service and Relationship Management

  • Oversee customer service standards and service excellence initiatives.
  • Ensure timely resolution of customer inquiries, complaints, claims-related concerns, and investment service requests.
  • Strengthen relationship management practices for individual, corporate, institutional, and high-net-worth clients.
  • Establish service-level agreements (SLAs) and escalation procedures across customer-facing departments.

Employee Experience and Organizational Culture

  • Develop initiatives that improve employee engagement and internal service culture.
  • Promote collaboration between departments to deliver consistent customer experiences.
  • Support employee training and development in customer service, communication, relationship management, and service excellence.
  • Align employee experience initiatives with customer experience objectives.

Governance, Risk and Compliance

  • Ensure customer experience practices comply with applicable insurance, investment, consumer protection, data privacy, and financial services regulations.
  • Work with compliance and risk teams to address customer-related regulatory concerns.
  • Promote transparent communication, fair treatment, responsible product information, and ethical customer engagement.
  • Establish processes for monitoring and resolving customer complaints and service-related risks.

Leadership and Performance Management

  • Lead and develop customer experience, customer service, and service transformation teams.
  • Establish departmental objectives, budgets, KPIs, and performance management frameworks.
  • Present customer experience performance reports and strategic recommendations to the CEO and Board.
  • Collaborate with senior executives to integrate customer experience priorities into business strategy.

3. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Finance, Management, Customer Experience, or a related field.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA) or a relevant discipline preferred.
  • 10–15+ years of progressive experience in customer experience, customer service, operations, client relationship management, or business transformation.
  • At least 5 years in a senior leadership or executive management position.
  • Experience in insurance, banking, investment management, wealth management, financial services, or other regulated service industries.
  • Demonstrated success in developing and implementing customer experience strategies.
  • Strong knowledge of customer journey mapping, CRM platforms, customer analytics, NPS, CSAT, and service quality management.
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams and large-scale service improvement initiatives.
  • Strong strategic thinking, communication, stakeholder management, and leadership capabilities.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

- Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT).

- Net Promoter Score (NPS).

  • Customer retention and policy renewal rates.
  • Customer attrition and churn reduction.
  • Customer complaint resolution time and satisfaction.

- First Contact Resolution (FCR) rate.

  • Digital channel adoption and self-service utilization.
  • Customer onboarding and service turnaround time.
  • Customer lifetime value and relationship growth.
  • Employee engagement and service culture improvement.
  • Compliance with customer service standards and regulatory requirements.
