jobs.description:
The salary range for this role is $2,800 - $6,000 per month (Gross in USD)

About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

About the Role:

We are seeking a talented and motivated Software Engineer with a unique blend of accounting experience who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. This role is tailored for professionals who started their careers in accounting but pivoted to engineering and now want to leverage their domain expertise to solve technical challenges in fintech. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. The Software Engineer will assist us with the design, development, and installation of software solutions. Your duties will include development, writing code, and documenting functionality. You should be able to build high-quality, innovative and fully performing software in compliance with coding standards and technical design.

Compensation:

For this mid-level development role, with 3-7 years of experience, the compensation range is $2,800 - $6,000 USD per month. This range is designed to reflect the skills, experience, and value brought to the team, ensuring competitive and fair pay within the industry.

Interview Process

We believe transparency is important at Sezzle. Regularly providing feedback while setting expectations is part of our culture starting with the interview process. Advancement through each step is not guaranteed.

  • Application submitted (you are here)
  • Wonderlic test (30-40 min)
  • Coding assessment (~1.5 hours)
  • Interview with recruiters (30 min)
  • Interview with engineers (1 hour)
  • Interview with engineering leadership (30-45 min)
  • Offer!

Sezzle Technical Stack:

  • Golang backend, React / React Native front-end
  • Grafana / Loki / Prometheus metrics
  • Kubernetes
  • AWS
  • Amazon Aurora (MySQL) RDS
  • Gitlab CI/CD deployments
  • Unit, Integration, and end-to-end testing

What You'll Do:

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to enhance and maintain software solutions for financial processes.
  • Be an integral part of the software development lifecycle.
  • Work as an integrated team member developing new features.
  • Leverage accounting background to identify gaps and improve automation and reconciliation workflows.
  • Evaluate and deploy software tools, processes, and metrics.
  • Provide support and consulting on software systems usage.
  • Ensure compliance with project plans and industry standards.

What We Look For:

  • Prior experience as an accountant or financial analyst.
  • Solid understanding of financial operations such as reconciliation, reporting, and compliance.
  • Proficient in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Java, Go) and familiar with database systems like MySQL or PostgreSQL.
  • Experience with backend API development.
  • Experience with relational database storage and retrieval.
  • Familiarity with software engineering tools, software development methodology, and release processes.
  • Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication.
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

Sezzle’s Technology Stack:

  • Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python
  • Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native
  • Backend: Golang
  • Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch
  • DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes
  • Version Control: Git
  • CI/CD: Gitlab
  • Testing: Developer-driven, focus on automated unit, integration, and end-to-end tests
  • Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!

About You:

  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome:

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

Role: Support Engineer

Location: Remote, US

Contract: Permanent, Full-Time

Hours: 40 hours per week

Salary: $55,000 - $65,000 per annum, plus benefits including: health, vision/dental insurance; disability, vacation, sickness, 401K

Kinly is a leading integrator of audio-visual and unified communications solutions, and the largest in Europe, serving as a globally trusted technology advisor to leading organisations. For more than 25 years, we have been designing, developing, integrating and supporting complex audiovisual solutions and businesses rely on us to deliver consistently secure and flexible meeting experiences.

The AV/UC Support Engineer is a frontline role on Kinly's global Service Desk, resolving hardware, software, and network issues across managed audio-visual and unified communications (UC) environments. The role blends traditional AV troubleshooting with cloud-based room management, remote monitoring, and proactive incident prevention — reflecting how modern meeting-room estates are supported at scale. Fast, first-contact resolution and clear communication with end users are central to the role and to Kinly's SLA commitments.

Key Responsibilities:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the following. Other duties may be assigned; reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities.

  • Provide phone, chat, video, and remote-session support for AV and video-conferencing incidents, performing Tier 2 diagnosis using ServiceNow (SNOW) and designated client tools and runbooks.

  • Troubleshoot commercial AV and UC platforms and appliances, including:

    • Microsoft Teams Rooms (Windows and Android) and Teams Rooms Pro management

    • Zoom Rooms, Zoom Workplace, and Zoom device management

    • Cisco Webex Devices, Webex Control Hub, and RoomOS-based appliances

    • Crestron Flex, DM NVX/AV-over-IP, XiO Cloud, and room scheduling panels

    • Poly (HP) video endpoints and Poly Lens cloud management

    • Logitech Rally/Sight endpoints and Logitech Sync

    • Neat and Lenovo ThinkSmart appliances and their respective management portals

    • Biamp Tesira and Q-SYS audio DSP platforms; Shure and Sennheiser microphone systems

  • Use cloud device-management and remote-monitoring platforms (e.g., XiO Cloud, Poly Lens, Logitech Sync, Cisco Control Hub, Teams admin center) to proactively identify and resolve issues before they become user-facing incidents.

  • Manage designated video-conferencing and AV facilities, including systems maintenance, moves/adds/changes, and administration to client service standards.

  • Pull usage analytics, health/issue reports, and KPI data from ServiceNow, Power BI dashboards, and platform-native reporting tools to support trend analysis and continuous improvement.

  • Deliver end-user training and white-glove support for VIP meetings, town halls, hybrid events, and executive spaces.

  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to other Support Desk and field AV/UC coordinators.

  • Maintain accurate room and equipment inventory in the CMDB during preventative-maintenance visits and asset audits.

  • Coordinate AV/UC support for scheduled client events (all-hands, town halls, board meetings, hybrid conferences).

  • Create and maintain user-facing documentation, quick-reference guides, and Kinly's internal knowledge base of AV/UC system documentation.

  • Perform low-to-mid-level network diagnostics on room and endpoint connectivity (VLAN, QoS, firewall/port checks) in coordination with network engineering.

  • Follow ITIL-aligned incident, request, and problem-management practices as part of Kinly's global service desk maturity framework.

Skills & Experience:

  • Excellent oral and written communication with technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strong problem-solving and structured troubleshooting skills.

  • Responsive, professional customer service across phone, chat, and video-support channels.

  • Effective teamwork; builds strong working relationships across regions and shifts.

  • Flexible to off-hour, on-call, or event-based support and occasional on-site redeployment.

  • Works effectively under pressure and independently with minimal supervision.

  • Committed to continuous learning as AV/UC platforms and cloud tools evolve.

  • Follows Kinly's operating standards for professional conduct and client-site presentation.

Education/Experience:

  • Prior Service Desk or technical support experience, ideally in AV, UC, or IT environments.

We serve the giving community worldwide with a comprehensive suite of solutions spanning grant management, community foundation software, and giving analytics.

We're a unified company shaped by strong roots across our product portfolio, and we operate with intention and purpose. Our team of ~350 people across six countries is connected by a shared North Star: to be the trusted partner and strategic advisor to the communities we serve.

You’ll provide prompt, professional, and knowledgeable technical support to help mission-driven organizations succeed with our software. This role combines troubleshooting expertise with a passion for customer success, operating as a technical problem-solver and customer advocate who helps organizations achieve their missions more efficiently and effectively.

Our global network of talent is supported by physical office hubs and virtual collaboration, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation and growth thrive.
  • With office locations in Bozeman, MT, Toronto, Canada, and Dublin, Ireland, you'll be part of a globally connected team. Whether you're working remotely or from one of our office locations, you'll be contributing to a vibrant, collaborative culture focused on driving meaningful impact across the world.

  • Some travel may be required (estimated less than 10%).
  • Other duties as assigned.

WhatYou’llNeed:

Required qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Technology, Engineering, Sciences, Mathematics (STEM) field.
  • 1–2 years of experience in a customer-facing technical support, or SaaS support role.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical users.
  • Comfortable learning new software platforms quickly; prior exposure to SaaS, CRM, or grants management tools is a plus.
  • Solid troubleshooting instincts - able to isolate a problem, test hypotheses, and document findings.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail when managing a queue of concurrent tickets.
  • Demonstrable success in thinking strategically, executing tactically, while providing consistent and high levels of client satisfaction and retention in a fast-paced environment.  
  • Comfortable working in a metric-driven environment.

Required Technical Skills

  • Fundamental knowledge of databases and SQL - able to read basic queries, understand table relationships, and assist with simple data troubleshooting.
  • Field data storage concepts - understanding of data types, field mappings, and how data is stored and retrieved in database systems.
  • Basic HTML/CSS knowledge - able to read and understand HTML/CSS code, troubleshoot formatting issues.
  • JavaScript fundamentals - able to recognize JavaScript syntax, understand basic functions and logic, and troubleshoot workflow automations.

  • Integration protocols and SSO (Single Sign-On) - familiarity with how external systems connect via integrations, including SMTP, SFTP, API connections, and authentication methods.

Preferred qualifications

The Opportunity:

CACI is seeking an Offensive Security Technical Lead to own technical delivery across the penetration-testing and red-team workstreams. This position will provide continuous technical assessment support for full‑time, proactive testing of externally and internally visible federal cyber assets. This expands federal visibility by conducting continual assessments of .gov domains, subdomains, and internet‑facing assets to uncover unknown exposures, validate vulnerabilities, and provide agencies with actionable remediation guidance. The Technical Lead establishes methodology, approves complex plans and rules of engagement, governs technical risk, allocates specialized expertise across concurrent assessments, resolves escalations, and accepts final technical deliverables while remaining credible and hands-on with offensive-security tradecraft. This role supports the Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (CDM) Program’s mission to safeguard and secure cyberspace in an environment where the threat of cyber-attack is continuously growing and evolving and is responsible for enhancing the security, resilience, and reliability of the Nation’s cyber and communications infrastructure. The CDM Program defends the United States (U.S.) Federal Information Technology (IT) networks from cybersecurity threats by providing continuous monitoring sensors (tools), diagnosis, mitigation tools, and associated services to strengthen the security posture of Government networks.

Responsibilities:

  • Guide the technical team, assign scarce specialties, mentor staff, conduct technical readiness reviews, and resolve complex cross-domain problems.
  • Provide hands-on support for the most difficult network, application, Active Directory/identity, cloud, exploit-development, adversary-infrastructure, and defense-evasion challenges.
  • Own final technical quality and acceptance for assessment reports, attack-path narratives, severity decisions, remediation recommendations, customer out-briefs, and purple-team scenarios.
  • Lead technical customer discussions, communicate mission and business risk, and coordinate with project management on schedule, staffing, dependencies, and issue escalation without assuming administrative PM ownership.
  • Capture lessons learned, measure technical quality and repeatability, and evolve the capability as customer processes and tools become known.

Required:

• U.S. citizenship is required.

  • Eight or more years of progressively responsible offensive-security experience, including significant hands-on penetration testing and red-team/adversary-emulation delivery.

  • Expert ability to scope and govern safe testing across enterprise networks, applications/APIs, Windows/Active Directory and identity, Linux, AWS/Azure, external attack surfaces, and production environments.
  • Demonstrated technical authority in rules of engagement, operational risk, deconfliction, exploit validation, evidence quality, severity decisions, report acceptance, and customer out-briefing.
  • Strong scripting, automation, or tool-development capability and the judgment to approve or reject high-risk technical methods.

Desired:

Job Summary

The Outpatient Coder is responsible for accurately assigning ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS codes for outpatient services, including emergency department visits, outpatient surgeries, observation stays, interventional radiology, wound care, and ancillary procedures. This role ensures compliance with coding guidelines, regulatory requirements, and corporate billing policies, while contributing to accurate reimbursement and data integrity. The Outpatient Coder reviews medical records and applies appropriate codes within hospital coding systems.

Essential Functions
  • Reviews and assigns appropriate ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS codes for outpatient records, ensuring compliance with coding and billing regulations.
  • Codes a variety of outpatient encounters, including observation stays, outpatient surgeries, interventional radiology, cardiac catheterization, emergency department visits, wound care, and ancillary services.
  • Applies correct coding guidelines and payer-specific policies, ensuring adherence to LCD/NCD (Local Coverage Determination/National Coverage Determination) requirements.
  • Resolves coding edits and denials, identifying and correcting discrepancies while maintaining compliance with corporate and regulatory standards.
  • Maintains coding productivity and accuracy standards, achieving a 95% coding accuracy rate and meeting corporate benchmarks.
  • Consults with the Manager or other subject matter experts to resolve complex coding issues and discrepancies.
  • Collaborates with Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI) specialists and billing teams, ensuring complete and accurate coding and documentation.
  • Ensures adherence to HIPAA privacy and security standards, maintaining confidentiality of patient records.
  • Utilizes hospital coding software and related tools to ensure accuracy and compliance with corporate policies.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.
Qualifications
  • H.S. Diploma or GED required
  • Associate Degree in Health Information Management, Medical Coding, or a related field preferred or
  • One (1) year coding certification in Health Information Management preferred
  • 1-3 years of outpatient coding experience in an acute care hospital or healthcare system required
  • Experience coding emergency department visits, outpatient procedures, interventional radiology, and/or ambulatory surgery preferred
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
  • Strong knowledge of ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS coding principles and outpatient reimbursement methodologies.
  • Understanding of Local Coverage Determination (LCD), National Coverage Determination (NCD), and payer-specific coding guidelines.
  • Experience with electronic health record (EHR) systems and coding software (e.g., 3M, Meditech, Epic, Cerner).
  • Ability to analyze and resolve coding edits, rejections, and denials efficiently.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to collaborate with CDI teams and billing departments.
  • Knowledge of HIPAA regulations and patient privacy standards.
Licenses and Certifications
  • Certified Coding Specialist (CCS) – AHIMA required or
  • CCA - Certified Coding Associate required or
  • Certified Outpatient Coder (COC) – AAPC required
  • RHIA - Registered Health Information Administrator preferred or
  • RHIT - Registered Health Information Technician preferred

Director of Outsourced Managed Services

Financial Aid Services (FAS)

About Us

At Financial Aid Services (FAS), we’re more than a consulting firm — we’re the trusted partner for colleges and universities navigating the complexities of financial aid. Our expert consultants help institutions strengthen their operations, optimize technology, maintain compliance, and fill critical leadership roles.

Our work is dynamic, impactful, and fast-paced — no two days are the same. Projects range from short-term assignments to year-long engagements, requiring strategic resource planning to match the right expertise with each institution’s needs.

The Opportunity to Make an Impact Beyond a Single Institution

FAS is seeking an experienced financial aid and higher education business leader to oversee and grow our Outsourced Managed Services division. This opportunity is ideal for professionals who have served as Directors, Executive Directors, Associate Vice Presidents, Vice Presidents, or other senior leaders within financial aid and are interested in applying their expertise across multiple colleges and universities nationwide.

As Director of Outsourced Managed Services, you will lead a current team of 14 professionals supporting more than 20 active client engagements with the goal of expanding to 50+ clients in the next 24 months. You will work closely with FAS executive leadership to strengthen operational performance, ensure regulatory compliance, improve organizational effectiveness, and leverage technology, automation, and AI to modernize our processing operations.

This leader will play a critical role in transforming the financial aid operations of our clients into a strategic driver of enrollment growth and financial health. You will be responsible for re-engineering workflows, accelerating file turnaround times, standardizing service delivery, and driving innovation through AI-enabled solutions. The successful candidate brings deep financial aid expertise, strong operational leadership skills, a passion for client success, and the ability to build trusted partnerships with clients and internal teams.

What You'll Do

Operational Leadership

  • Lead and develop a team of 14 staff currently, including four Project Leads, providing vision, coaching, mentorship, and a high performance culture of accountability.
  • Manage processing operations across 20 active client engagements with the expectation of growing and scaling the operation to serve 50+ clients in the next 24 months.
  • Monitor project timelines, deliverables, quality standards, and client satisfaction metrics.
  • Identify and proactively address operational risks, resource constraints, and delivery challenges.
  • Optimize consultant utilization and minimize bench time while maintaining exceptional service quality.
  • Review and determine staffing allocations.
  • Develop a flexible workforce strategy that balances full-time employees and independent contractors to optimize utilization, control costs, and support business growth.
  • Monitor progress of all active processing engagements to ensure project milestones, deliverable deadlines, and quality standards are consistently achieved.
  • Re-engineer processing operations for speed, scalability, and consistency while maintaining strong compliance controls.
  • Establish performance targets and operational workflows designed to reduce file turnaround times and improve responsiveness to client needs.
  • Own and continuously evolve the Analyst Training and Performance Enablement program, including onboarding, skills development, knowledge management, coaching, performance improvement plans, and career progression pathways to build a scalable, high-performing workforce.

Process Excellence & Standardization

  • Document, maintain, and continuously improve standard operating procedures (SOPs) across all processing services.
  • Standardize service delivery methodologies for key functional areas including to ensure consistency and quality across all client engagements:
    • Verification
    • Packaging and Awarding
    • Return of Title IV Funds (R2T4)
    • Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP)
    • Reconciliation
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives that increase productivity, throughput, and overall operational effectiveness.

Performance Management & Reporting

  • Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) within the FASTrax 2.0 platform, including:
    • Utilization
    • Productivity
    • Cycle times
    • Turnaround times
    • Quality assurance
  • Deliver data-driven operational insights and recommendations to executive leadership.
  • Work with finance team to monitor engagement profitability, staffing efficiency, and resource utilization trends.
  • Maintain operational dashboards to support performance management and decision-making in FASTrax 2.0.

Innovation & Technology

  • Lead the transformation of the Processing Services division through technology, automation, and AI-enabled solutions.
  • Identify workflow automation opportunities to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and increase operational capacity.
  • Leverage AI to streamline processing activities, accelerate decision-making, and improve service delivery.
  • Evaluate and standardize workflows to eliminate inefficiencies and create faster, more consistent outcomes for clients.
  • Drive initiatives to accelerate file turnaround times while maintaining high levels of quality and compliance.
  • Champion innovation and a culture of continuous improvement across the Processing Services division.

Client Partnership & Service Delivery

  • Serve as a senior escalation point for client concerns and operational issues.
  • Partner with institutions to ensure successful delivery of contracted services.
  • Collaborate with project teams to meet client expectations and ensure high-quality outcomes.
  • Understand long-term client goals and how our services need to adapt to meet those future client challenges and opportunities.
  • Foster long-term client relationships built on trust, responsiveness, and measurable results.

Compliance & Quality Assurance

  • Maintain deep knowledge of federal financial aid regulations and industry best practices.
  • Support internal quality control reviews and annual audit initiative.
  • Monitor compliance trends and recommend enhancements to mitigate institutional and operational risk.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, accuracy, and regulatory excellence.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive financial aid leadership experience.
  • Experience leading financial aid operations at a college, university, system office, or higher education organization.
  • Demonstrated success managing teams, workflows, complex operational initiatives that include change management.
  • Deep understanding of Title IV regulations and financial aid administration.
  • Strong project management, organizational, and change management skills.
  • Demonstrated success leveraging technology to drive efficiency gains and operational excellence.
  • Proven ability to lead high-performing teams in a remote environment.
  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and client management skills.
  • Experience using operational data and metrics to drive performance improvement.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Multi-campus, multi-system, or consulting experience.
  • Experience leading process improvement initiatives.
  • Experience implementing automation or workflow redesign solutions.
  • Familiarity with Ellucian Banner, Colleague, PeopleSoft, Jenzabar, CampusNexus, or other SIS platforms.
  • Experience developing KPIs, operational dashboards, and performance management frameworks.
  • Demonstrated ability to scale operations while maintaining quality and compliance standards.

Why Join FAS?

At FAS, you'll have the opportunity to influence financial aid operations nationwide while working alongside a team of dedicated higher education professionals. You'll help shape the future of our Processing Services organization, drive operational excellence, and build innovative solutions that improve outcomes for institutions and students alike.

We offer:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Remote work flexibility
  • Comprehensive benefits package
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Collaborative and entrepreneurial culture
  • Opportunity to lead organizational transformation through technology and AI

jobs.description:
Overview

We are seeking a Global Privacy Program Director with 7+ years of relevant privacy experience to coordinate day-to-day privacy program operations and implementation under the direction of the Deputy General Counsel, Global Privacy, Cybersecurity and AI Governance Officer; Chief Privacy Officer. This full-time role requires a highly responsive, prepared, technology-aware, and business-oriented privacy professional who can translate privacy strategy, regulatory obligations, emerging AI requirements, and leadership priorities into practical controls, policies, workflows, notices, and operating guidance across the United States, EMEA, and other global markets. Consilio is a global legal services and eDiscovery solutions provider supporting large corporations and law firms across the United States, United Kingdom, Europe and Asia Pacific.

The Director, Global Privacy Program will report to the Deputy General Counsel, Global Privacy, Cybersecurity and AI Governance Officer; Chief Privacy Officer. The successful candidate will be responsible for assisting with day-to-day program operations, operational delivery, and cross-functional implementation, with program direction, strategy, executive reporting, final risk decisions, and enterprise privacy accountability retained by the Chief Privacy Officer.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

  • Coordinate day-to-day execution and continuous improvement of Consilio’s global privacy and data-protection program in alignment with the strategy, priorities, and risk direction set by the Chief Privacy Officer, including policies, standards, procedures, controls, issue tracking, testing, and remediation.
  • Implement privacy governance processes, decision records, escalation pathways, and accountability mechanisms approved by the Chief Privacy Officer to ensure privacy issues are identified, owned, tracked, and resolved in a timely manner.
  • Operate with a high degree of independence on day-to-day program execution, using sound judgment to prioritize work, make practical recommendations, and escalate material legal, regulatory, client, or enterprise risk issues to the Chief Privacy Officer.
  • Provide practical program support and operational guidance on GDPR, UK GDPR, U.S. state privacy laws, and other global privacy and data protection requirements.
  • Assist in tracking privacy, cybersecurity, AI, and data-governance developments and prepare practical recommendations, roadmap updates, training, templates, notices, and operational control enhancements for review and direction by the Chief Privacy Officer.
  • Apply emerging AI laws, regulations, regulatory guidance, and company AI governance requirements to privacy program activities, including policy updates, just-in-time notices, DPIA/PIA enhancements, data-use reviews, and practical evaluation of AI-related privacy risk.
  • Partner closely with Legal, Information Security, IT, Product, Operations, Sales, HR, and client-facing teams to embed privacy-by-design into new products, services, client solutions, vendor relationships, and internal initiatives.
  • Partner effectively with regional stakeholders, including EMEA Legal, Security, Operations, and client-facing teams, to address GDPR, UK GDPR, cross-border transfer, and other regional privacy requirements as part of the broader global privacy program.
  • Maintain, refresh, and mature core privacy program elements on an ongoing basis, including records of processing, data maps, DPIA/PIA processes, privacy notices, consent and rights processes, data retention, cross-border transfer assessments, training, audit readiness, and related transfer compliance controls.
  • Identify opportunities to automate privacy operations where practical, including intake, workflow, reporting, evidence collection, reminders, control tracking, and other repeatable privacy program activities.
  • Develop and maintain global privacy policies, procedures, playbooks, templates, training, and communications that are clear, practical, and aligned with business operations.
  • Support operational privacy risk review in commercial, client, vendor, supplier, and technology matters, including DPAs, data processing terms, security/privacy questionnaires, data-use restrictions, audit rights, AI-enabled services, just-in-time notices, and sensitive data use cases, with escalation of material privacy, AI, client, regulatory, or enterprise risk issues to the Chief Privacy Officer.
  • Support privacy incident readiness and response by partnering with Legal, Security, and business stakeholders to assess risk, coordinate response activities, and document outcomes.
  • Maintain privacy program metrics, dashboards, control testing, remediation plans, and risk reporting inputs to support Chief Privacy Officer-led executive readouts, roadmap decisions, and leadership reporting.
  • Support regulatory inquiries, investigations, audits, and information requests by coordinating documentation, facts, timelines, evidence, and draft response materials for Chief Privacy Officer review and direction.

Qualifications

  • Minimum 7+ years of relevant privacy, data protection, compliance, technology law, and/or privacy operations experience.
  • Deep, practical knowledge of GDPR is required, together with strong familiarity with UK GDPR, EMEA privacy requirements, U.S. state privacy laws, international transfer requirements, data governance, privacy operations, and privacy risk management.
  • IAPP certification strongly preferred, including CIPP/E and/or CIPP/US; CIPM, CIPT, or other recognized privacy, data protection, or security certifications are a plus.
  • D., equivalent legal qualification, or comparable advanced privacy, compliance, or technology credential preferred.
  • Excellent drafting, communication, and training skills, with the ability to translate complex privacy requirements into clear, actionable guidance for legal, technical, and business audiences.
  • Strong business judgment and professional presence, with the ability to support leadership discussions, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and elevate issues requiring Chief Privacy Officer direction.
  • Working familiarity with AI governance concepts and emerging AI regulatory frameworks, with the ability and interest to develop deeper fluency and apply AI requirements to privacy policies, notices, assessments, and risk reviews.
  • Ability to interpret regulatory guidance and enforcement trends and convert them into practical, risk-based recommendations for business, legal, security, and technology stakeholders.
  • Experience supporting interactions with privacy, data protection, or other relevant regulators, including preparing factual summaries, documentation, evidence, and draft response materials for senior legal review.

Key Experience

  • Significant experience improving and managing day-to-day privacy program operations, including governance forums, policy frameworks, controls, issue management, regulatory change management, metrics, roadmap support, and reporting inputs.
  • Experience building, scaling, maintaining, or materially improving privacy program components such as DPIAs/PIAs, data mapping, records of processing, privacy notices, consent and preference processes, DSARs, vendor privacy reviews, third-party risk, training, audits, readiness assessments, and recurring control refresh processes.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting EMEA operations and stakeholders is required; experience collaborating across UK, EU, APAC, and U.S. teams is strongly preferred.

Consilio’s True North Values

Client Experience

We listen for the “why,” clearly define success, maintain accountability, and go the extra distance to create moments that matter.

Collaboration

We treat everyone with respect, welcome diverse views, and partner across geographies, generations, and teams, rallying around final decisions.

Innovation

We are always curious. We challenge the status quo, experiment to fail forward, and build for the future.

Grit

We focus on what matters. We work with passion and persistence, think like an owner, and deliver results we’re proud of.

jobs.excerpt: Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency.
jobs.description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

The Architecture team at Tenstorrent is designing the central compute chiplet that powers our next generation automotive SoC. This role is about turning real world automotive and safety requirements into architecture that performs, scales, and ships fast and reliably. If you think silicon design should start with clarity and end with confidence, this is where your experience makes the biggest impact.

This role is remote, based in Munich, Germany.

We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.

Who You Are

  • Approach design with a systems mindset, always thinking in trade offs, not just specs and block diagrams.
  • Bring deep knowledge of SoC architecture, from interconnects and I/O to memory and CPUs.
  • Confident working within performance, power, and reliability constraints.
  • Familiar with, or eager to dive into, functional safety, ISO 26262, and automotive grade design challenges.

What We Need

  • Someone to architect and specify one or more chiplets in the robotics and automotive family.
  • 5+ years of experience translating high level requirements into detailed architectural direction.
  • Ability to identify impactful features that boost PPA, safety, and reliability, without adding unnecessary complexity.
  • Willingness to collaborate across design, verification, software, and systems teams to keep execution moving.

What You Will Learn

  • What it takes to architect a chiplet based SoC for automotive applications.
  • How functional safety and reliability shape every design decision.
  • How to integrate complex IP blocks and CPU subsystems into a coherent, shippable product.
  • Why silicon architecture is a cross functional discipline, not just a collection of isolated blocks.

Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.

This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology. Due to U.S. export laws, including those codified in the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the Company is required to ensure compliance with these laws when transferring technology to nationals of certain countries (such as EAR Country Groups D:1, E1, and E2). These requirements apply to persons located in the U.S. and all countries outside the U.S. As the position offered will have direct and/or indirect access to information, systems, or technologies subject to these laws, the offer may be contingent upon your citizenship/permanent residency status or ability to obtain prior license approval from the U.S. Commerce Department or applicable federal agency. If employment is not possible due to U.S. export laws, any offer of employment will be rescinded.

jobs.title: Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs
jobs.excerpt: GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good.
jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find.

We’re hiring a Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs to lead how GiveWell’s work is represented in the media and in public conversations. You will set our strategy, build trusted relationships with journalists and other influential voices, pursue opportunities that increase understanding of GiveWell’s work, and lead our external response in fast-moving situations.

This role reports to Steven Profaizer, our Vice President of Communications, and will lead a small and growing team. This is one of three new communications leadership roles, alongside a Senior Communications Officer, Strategic Communications and a Senior Communications Officer, Editorial & Production.

About the role

Both our research and impact are expanding. Last year, we directed more than $400 million to highly cost-effective programs that save and improve lives. This year, we expect our grantmaking to approach, and possibly exceed, $1 billion.

To build toward the communications capacity this next stage requires, we are rapidly expanding our team. Together with the Vice President of Communications, the three new Senior Communications Officers will form GiveWell’s communications leadership team. Each leader will own their function, but much of the work that matters most—like team strategies, major initiatives, partnership campaigns, and how we present the organization as a whole—will involve all three. We will expect this group to set shared priorities and work closely together to achieve the team’s goals.

In this hands-on leadership position, you’ll own how and where GiveWell engages in media and public conversations, with end-to-end responsibility for this emerging function. You’ll set its strategy, hire and develop its people, build its systems, and personally own its hardest and most consequential work. This is an opportunity to build, not just inherit, an important function at a critical point in GiveWell’s development. You’ll start with a small team and grow it over time.

While this role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level, we may consider hiring an exceptional candidate as a Communications Director—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.

What You'll Do

As Senior Communications Officer, Media & Public Affairs, you will combine long-term strategy and relationship-building with the ability to respond quickly and exercise sound judgment in sensitive or fast-moving situations.

Specific duties will include:

  • Set GiveWell’s strategy across media, thought-leader engagement, online communities, public forums and events, and other earned communications opportunities—including deciding where and when GiveWell should participate and overseeing those engagements.
  • Build and maintain high-trust relationships with journalists, editors, podcast hosts, event organizers, thought leaders, subject-matter experts, and other influential external stakeholders.
  • Identify, develop, and pitch substantive stories, event opportunities, and thought-leadership ideas that extend understanding of GiveWell’s work.
  • Own inbound media engagement, including situations that require rapid responses, close coordination with subject-matter experts, and careful judgment about what GiveWell can responsibly say—and about which responses need escalation.
  • Build and maintain GiveWell’s readiness for sensitive or fast-moving situations, monitor emerging issues in media and public conversations, and lead our external response when needed in partnership with others.
  • Advise GiveWell’s leadership on external opportunities and relationships, and prepare senior leaders and subject-matter experts for interviews, speaking engagements, and other public appearances.
  • Exercise sound judgment about when and how GiveWell should enter public conversations, including evaluating likely value, reputational considerations, and communications risks.
  • Evaluate and help shape public-facing communications partnerships, advising on which opportunities GiveWell should pursue and how we should participate.
  • Serve as a spokesperson for GiveWell in select media interviews, events, and other public forums, communicating our perspective clearly, accurately, and with sound judgment.
  • Work with grantees and other partners on press releases and other media-facing communications involving GiveWell or our shared work.
  • Manage and develop one or two team members initially, and build the relationships, systems, and additional capacity the function will need over time.

About You

You are skilled at using communications to help people understand complex ideas, build trust, and take action. You are comfortable being accountable for outcomes, making consequential decisions with limited oversight, and knowing which decisions genuinely require escalation.

You are energized by intellectually demanding work, and the challenges of creating engaging communications within a careful and precise style. You can engage deeply with GiveWell’s research, and you are comfortable understanding and communicating about data in detail. You have a long track record of getting up to speed quickly on complex subject matter and carefully communicating to a very high standard. You can build a compelling narrative that is entirely factual, representing what is known and unknown without overstating or hedging into vagueness—and you find the idea of working with GiveWell’s exacting communications standards exciting rather than limiting.

Your background includes significant experience leading communications in complex, high-stakes environments. This should include 10+ years of experience in media relations, thought leadership, and public engagement. You have deep experience owning that work end to end, not just contributing to it. You’ve remained a hands-on leader who enjoys the work itself, as well as the strategy and systems behind it.

You know how journalists, influential voices, events, and other public forums shape how organizations and ideas are understood. You have a demonstrated ability to build meaningful external relationships, identify opportunities worth pursuing, personally represent an organization’s perspective, and navigate public-facing situations in which context is limited, timelines are short, and judgment matters. Much of this should be work you executed yourself, in addition to work you directed. Experience in settings where precision and credibility were at least as important as reach is a strong signal of fit.

In addition to demonstrated expertise in the duties listed above, you should have:

  • Exceptional communications judgment, including the ability to understand audience, context, risk, timing, and the underlying substance of a message.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to quickly make complex ideas clear and compelling without sacrificing rigor or nuance.
  • A track record of building and leading: you have created or substantially rebuilt a team or function—not only run ones you inherited—and you have hired, developed, and managed people.
  • Recent, hands-on excellence at your craft: you can point to work from the past few years that you personally produced or substantially shaped.
  • Experience producing communications that are direct and factual while being engaging and effective with their target audiences—work that succeeds through substance and clarity rather than embellishment.
  • Intellectual curiosity and the ability to engage deeply with GiveWell’s research and ideas, even without prior experience in our giving areas.
  • Experience advising executives or other senior decision-makers directly.
  • Strong alignment with GiveWell’s mission and values, including truth-seeking, transparency, and a commitment to communicating accurately and thoughtfully.

We also think these qualities will help you do well in the role and at GiveWell:

  • People who can develop a strong point of view and hold it with confidence, but remain genuinely open to challenge, new information, and better ideas.
  • Self-starters who take ownership, are comfortable creating structure in an evolving environment, and can make thoughtful decisions without always having complete information.
  • People who are proactive and anticipatory, who identify opportunities, risks, bottlenecks, and communications needs before they become obvious.
  • Collaborative leaders who raise the quality of the work around them and build strong relationships across teams.
  • People who coordinate well with peers, resolve dependencies and disagreements, and make shared work clearer rather than more complicated.

Key Questions & Information

What are some of the reasons I might not like this role?

  • You want to step into a mature function with established systems, rather than build one while you run it.
  • You do best with clear direction and established priorities. We’ll expect you to set most of your own, make most decisions yourself, and reach substantial autonomy within your first six months.
  • You prefer advising on communications to producing and being accountable for them.
  • You want sole ownership of an organization’s overarching communications strategy and brand. At GiveWell, the Vice President of Communications owns that direction; you would help shape it and lead your function within it.
  • You want to lead a large team from day one. This team is small today, and much of the most difficult work will be yours to do directly.
  • You find standards of precision and understatement limiting and frustrating. We work extremely hard to only communicate accurately what we know and what we don’t.

Can I apply to more than one of the Senior Communications Officer roles?

You can, but most people shouldn’t. We’re looking for deep expertise in these areas, and we expect most candidates with required expertise will be a clear fit for a single role. If you’re one of the few with real depth in more than one area, apply to both and tell us why. Otherwise, apply for the role you are most qualified for, and we’ll let you know if we think another role might suit you better.

What does this interview process entail?

We’ll use a combination of interviews, written exercises, and work trials to assess the qualities described above. We’ll share more specific details if we invite you to move forward to any of the following stages, but our current plan is:

  • Application
  • Interview with a member of the Talent Acquisition Team
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial
  • Interview with the Vice President of Communications
  • Values interview
  • Compensated, ~4-hour work trial with the Vice President of Communications
  • CEO interview and References

Note that you don’t need to submit a cover letter. We rely heavily on your resume and answers to the application questions below when we’re making early decisions. We encourage you to spend time responding to the application questions thoroughly and carefully.

Details

  • Team: You’ll report to our Vice President of Communications, collaborate closely with the two other Senior Communications Officers, and lead a small team that you’ll develop over time.
  • Compensation: This role is set at the Senior Communications Officer level. For an exceptional candidate, we may consider hiring at the Communications Director level—with greater expectations, responsibilities, and compensation.
    • NYC or the San Francisco Bay Area: $250,000
    • All other U.S. locations: $225,000
    • International: Custom based on location. We can give you a specific number at the penultimate stage of the hiring process.
  • Location: GiveWell’s staff work primarily remotely within the U.S. and abroad.
    • Offices: You are welcome but not required to work from our offices in Oakland, California, or Brooklyn, NYC.
    • International work: We are happy to employ staff internationally on a case-by-case basis. Given the managerial nature of this role, a successful candidate will need to work hours that have a certain minimum overlap with American working hours and the schedules of key coworkers.
  • Flexibility: We support and encourage flexible working, including flexible hours, working remotely, and working from the office when you choose. The majority of our staff, including senior management, work flexibly in one way or another.
  • Visa Sponsorship: If you want to work in the United States and need a work visa, we’ll do our best to sponsor it (and also cover up to 100% of relocation expenses on a case-by-case basis). Please note that government entities ultimately dictate our ability to sponsor visas.
  • Benefits: Our benefits include:
    • Fully funded health, dental, vision, and life insurance (we cover 100% of premiums within the US for you and any dependents)
    • Four weeks of paid time off per year
    • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave
    • Ergonomic home workstations or coworking space memberships
    • 403(b) retirement plan
  • Travel: Communications staff members should expect to attend three week-long retreats each year to bond with other team members and complete in-person work. Other domestic and international travel may be required, but isn’t expected to be a regular part of these roles. We’ll discuss travel obligations in more detail during late stages of the hiring process, and we’ll give reasonable consideration to staff who have family or other obligations.
  • Start date: We’d like a candidate to start as soon as possible after receiving an offer.

About GiveWell

GiveWell is dedicated to finding and evaluating highly cost-effective global health and development opportunities, and we publish all the work, reasoning, and uncertainties behind our funding decisions. Our giving funds enable donors to contribute to the most impactful and cost-effective programs our researchers identify.

GiveWell is one of the world’s largest private funders of global development efforts. Trusted annually by tens of thousands of donors, GiveWell searches for highly cost-effective programs that save or improve lives the most. Since 2007, more than 150,000 donors have given over $2.6 billion through GiveWell to the most promising programs its research has identified, which we estimate will save more than 340,000 lives.

GiveWell is most well-known for recommending a small number of Top Charities, which currently support seasonal malaria chemoprevention, insecticide-treated nets, vaccine incentivization, and vitamin A supplementation. However, most of our research capacity and grantmaking is devoted to cost-effective opportunities outside of those programs.

GiveWell grants have:

  • Helped governments navigate changes to the funding landscape and implement high-impact health programs, like HIV/syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant people in Zambia and Cameroon.
  • Sought to scope and scale promising interventions that don’t have clear existing implementers. We are supporting the Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Incubator to identify potentially cost-effective interventions and create programs that we would be excited to support in the future. For example, we funded a program to prevent tuberculosis among young children in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, India, that we co-designed with CHAI through the Incubator program.
  • Provided funding to ensure that programs that recently faced foreign aid funding cuts could continue, like healthcare support and malnutrition treatment in northern Cameroon.
  • Funded program delivery alongside strengthened monitoring and evaluation, as in our grants to support treatment of clubfoot and to evaluate the program.
  • Tested our assumptions and refined our understanding through further research and data collection, including improved estimates of disease burden and studies on the effect of water chlorination on mortality and the impact of a tree-planting program on farmers’ income.

We make our reasoning public and transparent so others can challenge it (sometimes we even pay people to point out our errors). We go to unusual lengths to check our assumptions and assess our impact, including funding research to address our uncertainties and gathering independent monitoring and evaluation data about the programs we support. We change our minds when the evidence demands it. For more about GiveWell, listen to Ezra Klein’s recent interview with GiveWell’s co-founder and CEO Elie Hassenfeld.

Additional information

We don’t want to miss candidates that could do great things at GiveWell. Practically, that means a GiveWell staff member reviews every application carefully, considering the whole picture of your background and potential. If you’re on the fence about applying because you meet some but not 100% of our preferred qualifications (some studies suggest this hesitation is especially common for women and people of color), we encourage you to apply anyway.

jobs.excerpt: If you are a passionate Full Stack Developer with expertise in Elixir, Phoenix and LiveView, and you're excited about revolutionizing the investment industry by crafting solutions for operational challenges and turning best practices into scalable, valuable products, Allocator One could be the perfect destination for your skills.
jobs.description:
If you are a passionate Full Stack Developer with expertise in Elixir, Phoenix and LiveView, and you're excited about revolutionizing the investment industry by crafting solutions for operational challenges and turning best practices into scalable, valuable products, Allocator One could be the perfect destination for your skills.

Come join our team where you'll play a crucial role in automating fund management and regulatory tasks, offering a transformative approach to the future of venture capital funds. You'll be working on all aspects of the application, from coding up user interfaces and components to building new endpoints or integrations. Our team has a good sense of humor and enjoys having fun. If you want to be part of this journey, keep reading!

We're on the lookout for individuals who've mastered either Elixir or React.js at a senior level, with at least a junior-level grasp of the other technology. If you're a senior pro in Ruby or Python and have a thirst for diving into Elixir, we're all ears and highly encourage you to apply.

As a member of our core team, you will work very closely with our founders, key stakeholders, and other experts. You will have the opportunity to learn from and contribute to the team's collective knowledge and expertise, and to participate in all aspects of the Allocator One value chain. The role will report into a Founding Partner.

Note: Allocator One is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. We offer the flexibility for this job to be performed remotely.

Allocator One

At Allocator One, we operate a distinctive fund model designed to invest in the most promising first-time fund managers worldwide while optimizing fees. With an eye on the highly favorable prospects for the 2023/2024 fund vintages, our team has accelerated its efforts to seize this unique opportunity. We pride ourselves on being the anchor investor of choice for exceptional first-time fund managers, offering them unparalleled access, expertise, and operational support.

Our focus on first-time fund managers

Allocator One's focus on first-time fund managers is driven by a simple yet compelling fact: historically, top-performing funds with assets under $50 million, led by emerging managers, have delivered returns that are more than 3 times higher over a 10-year horizon compared to their peers of larger fund sizes. Furthermore, the fund vintages of 2023/2024 in our pipeline are poised to enjoy an additional boost in returns. Venture capital funds that originate during economic recessions have consistently achieved returns that are 15%-30% higher compared to those raised in the preceding years, across various performance percentiles.

Optimizing fees and building Partnerships

We believe in optimizing fees while nurturing partnerships with first-time fund managers from the very beginning. Our aim is to enhance investment terms by actively contributing to the success of these funds. Allocator One has already established itself as a global brand in the realm of emerging managers, thanks to our extensive international investor network. In just two months since our launch, we've received over 300 applications, a testament to our commitment to supporting emerging talent. Our team goes beyond traditional investing; we offer to act as "co-builders," incorporating emerging managers into our unique Allocator One program, often likened to a "Y Combinator for Capital Allocators." We provide vital support in areas such as regulation, administration, and structure.

Our founding partners:

Our founders bring a wealth of experience and expertise to Allocator One:

  • Felix Staeritz: As the builder of category-leading corporate venture builder FoundersLane, Felix has an impressive track record of founding and exiting successful ventures. He is an active VC/PE investor and serves on the boards and advisory boards of esteemed organizations like the World Economic Forum (WEF), Fraunhofer, and various public and private companies.
  • Michael Ströck: Michael is a seasoned open source developer and entrepreneur with multiple successful exits to his name. He is an alumnus of Y Combinator and has transitioned from a CTO role to a successful investor. Michael has played a pivotal role in establishing three VC funds and is part of a family business now in its third generation.

Tasks

General responsibilities:

  • Implement new features on our web application
  • Solve complex programming challenges using functional programming languages (Elixir, in our case)
  • Develop new user-facing features using Elixir, Phoenix and LiveView
  • Build reusable components and front-end libraries for future use as specified by the UX team
  • Translate designs and wireframes into high-quality code integrated with the backend
  • Optimize components for maximum performance across a vast array of web-capable devices and browsers
  • Collaborate with the development team to develop a strategy that enables a great user experience
  • Continuously research new and best coding practices
  • Perform regular code reviews/PR reviews for your colleagues
  • Maintain existing code and fix bugs
  • Write unit, integration, and E2E tests

Requirements

Your skills and qualifications:

  • 5+ years of real-world experience in software development
  • Strong understanding of Elixir, Phoenix and LivewView in a production environment
  • Strong understanding of Elixir and LiveView
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • Good understanding of modern front-end build pipelines and tools
  • Experience with common front-end development tools such as Babel, Webpack, NPM, etc.
  • Ability to understand business requirements and translate them into technical requirements
  • Strong experience with HTML, CSS (we use Tailwind CSS ), and JavaScript
  • A strong desire to build beautiful end-user experiences that exceed expectation

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary
  • Potential for bonuses and equity
  • “No assholes allowed” company culture
  • Learn from and grow with experienced colleagues who are eager to share their knowledge

Hiring process:

Initial screen: This initial screen via video-call with a member of our team will be an opportunity for you to discuss your background and experience, and to ensure that you meet the minimum qualifications for the role and the job aligns with your expectations.

Interview with founding partners: If you are a strong candidate, you will be invited to participate in an interview with our founding partners. This will be an opportunity for you to learn more about the company's strategy and culture, and for the partners to get to know you better.

Case study and/or technical assessment during an work trial day: To get to know each other even better, we invite you to a work trial day, remotely. To assess your skills and knowledge, we may ask you to complete a case study or technical assessment.

After the final round interview, the team will review all of the candidates and make a decision on who to offer the position to. The hiring process can take several weeks, so please be patient as we review all of the applications and make a decision. If you are not selected for the role, we will notify you as soon as possible.

Sounds interesting? Then we look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.excerpt: Accelerate patient enrollment in clinical trials with SubjectWell/Clariness, helping patients gain access to life-changing medications.
jobs.description:
Accelerate patient enrollment in clinical trials with SubjectWell/Clariness, helping patients gain access to life-changing medications. We support biopharmaceutical companies and CROs in completing clinical trials faster so innovative treatments can reach patients sooner.

If you enjoy helping people and have strong communication skills, join our virtual team and contribute to meaningful medical research.

We are currently seeking a Freelance Study Coordinator to support our team in handling unscripted patient calls related to oncologyclinical trials. If you have a medical background, excellent communication skills, and experience in oncology or clinical research, this could be a great fit.

Tasks

About the role

As an Onco-Companion – Patient Recruitment, you will serve as a key link between cancer patients, their treating physicians, and clinical trial sites. Your mission is to help patients feel informed and supported as they consider research participation. You will not assess medical eligibility, but rather support understanding, encourage dialogue with care teams, and help coordinate communication with study sites.

As an Onco-Companion – Patient Recruitment, you will:

  • Conduct unscripted, empathetic conversations with cancer patients about clinical trial options.
  • Clearly explain the purpose, process, and risks of clinical trials using language that patients can understand.
  • Introduce relevant studies based on general criteria (e.g., cancer type, treatment setting, location).
  • Encourage informed discussions between patients and their treating physicians.
  • Coordinate initial outreach between physicians and research sites when a trial may be suitable.
  • Maintain ethical standards in communication and respect patient autonomy at all times.
  • Ensure proper documentation and confidentiality across all patient interactions.

Requirements

Education:

  • Medical degree (MD or equivalent) – required.

Experience:

  • At least 3 years of experience in oncology, clinical trials, or patient education.
  • Prior involvement in oncology trials or patient recruitment is a strong plus.
  • Familiarity with clinical trial workflows, patient navigation, or healthcare communication.

Languages:

  • Fluent German – required.
  • Professional English – required.
  • Professional Spanish - nice to have.

Location:

  • Remote, from anywhere.

Soft Skills & Attributes:

  • Empathetic, professional communicator comfortable with sensitive topics.
  • Strong organizational and coordination skills.
  • Able to explain medical concepts without providing clinical advice.
  • Respectful of ethical boundaries and patient autonomy.

Benefits

  • Remote freelance opportunity.
  • Competitive project-based compensation.
  • Meaningful work supporting cancer patients and clinical research.
  • Exposure to innovative oncology clinical trials.

Interested?

If you are a medical professional with oncology or clinical research experience and are passionate about patient-centered communication, we would love to hear from you!

Please submit your CV along with a brief summary of your relevant experience in oncology, clinical trials, or patient engagement. Qualified candidates will be contacted to discuss the project scope, expected availability, and next steps.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and respectful working environment and welcome applications from professionals of diverse backgrounds.

Join us in helping patients better understand their clinical trial options and connect with research opportunities that may shape the future of cancer care.

  • Demonstrated ability to drive the clinical deliverables of a study

PSI Medical Monitors provide medical input to global clinical studies and advise the teams and business partners, while always focusing on patients' safety and well-being.

Home-Based in Mexico

Responsibilities:

  • Acts as the primary point of contact for all parties on all trial-specific medical and safety-related questions
  • Provides input for responses to regulatory authorities and Institutional Review Boards (IRBs)/Independent Ethics Committees (IECs) on trial-specific medical and safety-related questions
  • Monitors trial participant safety
  • Participates in trial participant recruitment boost and retention activities
  • Presents on medical matters at kick-off and investigator meetings
  • Trains trial team in the therapeutic area and medical aspects of the protocol
  • Develops and reviews trial-specific documents within the scope of medical monitoring
  • Manages ongoing trial risks related to medical monitoring
  • Performs ongoing medical review of the operational clinical trial database; provides support to Medical Reviewer(s) assigned to the trial
  • Reviews protocol deviations
  • Reviews RAE reports, writes and/or reviews SAE narratives, supports Pharmacovigilance team with outstanding safety queries, interacts with sponsor on site safety issues
  • Reviews IND/SUSAR Safety Reports, updates/amendments to essential trial records, and annual IND reports with sponsor data (per sponsor request)
  • Participates in management of trial-related committees (e.g., independent data monitoring committee (IDMC)/adjudication committees) as described in the corresponding trial-specific charter(s)
  • Supports Pharmacovigilance, Medical Data Review and Data Management with reconciliation of safety and operational clinical trial databases
  • Reviews clinical study reports (CSRs), including safety narratives and tables, figures, and listings (TFLs)
  • Provides medical expertise on an as-needed basis in trials where medical monitoring is not a contract deliverable
  • Prepares for and participates in trial audits, follows up on audit findings
  • Participates in feasibility assessment of potential and ongoing trials in the country/region
  • Participates in bid defense meetings and other interactions with clients
  • Acts as a medical expert and provides therapeutic expertise to other PSI departments
  • Medical Doctor degree required
  • Experience as a practicing Gastroenterology (minimum of 10 years)
  • Clinical Research experience preferred
  • Proficiency with MS Office applications
  • Communication, presentation and analytical skills
  • Problem-solving, team and detail-oriented

As part of PSI's Medical Monitoring team, you will join our international group of medical professionals, build a career on the frontline of medical science and use your knowledge and expertise to help bring new medications to patients that need them.

PSI is a leading Contract Research Organization with more than 30 years in the industry, offering a perfect balance between stability and innovation to both clients and employees. We focus on delivering quality and on-time services across a variety of therapeutic indications.
